description: Falling like a curtain from the canopy, a wall of vines has interwoven itself so tightly that it blocks further passage in some directions.  Game trails twist their way through the rest of the trees, joining and parting like a meandering stream.

title: [[Seord Kerwaith, Mountainside]]
description: Mountain peaks, reminiscent of castle turrets, cast a persistent shadow over this region.  Rarely does the sun's warm embrace penetrate the chilly gloom.  Blasts of wind charge down the mountainsides to assault the glacial plain with unbridled fury.  Deep-throated rumbling echoes across the plain, the voice of the ancient icy river speaking on its slow, ponderous journey through the mountains.  Rising from the plain, a dark stone pillar stands resolute against nature's fury.
paths: Obvious paths: east, southeast, south, west, northwest.

title: [[Shambling Weald, Thicket]]
description: Underbrush crowds up against the taller trees, almost choking out any passage.  Forest creatures, however, have left their mark and a few twisting passages allow for travel deeper within the wilderness.

title: [[Seord Kerwaith, Mountainside]]
description: Resting in the shadow of taller peaks, the mountainside is subjected to frigid temperatures.  Cyclonic gusts tear down from the summit to race across the landscape, causing a banshee-like wail to issue forth from the deepest crevasses and chasms marring the terrain's icy blanket.  Blinding clouds of snow and ice, stirred by the constant winds, serve only to disorient the unwary.  A dark stone pillar, unstable as a result of glacial tremors, leans to one side.

Buried deep in night's shadow, the snowfield is subjected to freezing temperatures.  Cyclonic gusts tear down from the high peaks to race across the mountainside, causing a banshee-like wail to issue forth from the deepest crevasses and chasms marring the terrain's icy blanket.  Blinding clouds of snow and ice, stirred by the constant winds, serve only to disorient the unwary.  A dark stone pillar, unstable as a result of glacial tremors, leans into the wind.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast, south.

title: [[Seord Kerwaith, Mountainside]]
description: Towering mountain peaks rise high above this glacial plain, their tops lost in swirling clouds of windblown sleet.  A nearby peak casts a shadow over the ice field, creating a noticeable difference in temperature.  Large snowdrifts cover the mountainside, similar to the dunes of a desert and equally difficult to traverse.  The bleached bones of an unknown pack animal and its owner lie exposed at the base of a dark stone pillar.

Towering mountain peaks, majestic during the day, now cast malevolent shadows across the snowfield.  Already bitter cold during the day, the temperature plunges even lower as night falls.  Large drifts of snow cover the mountainside, similar to the dunes of a desert and equally difficult to traverse.  A mysterious dark stone pillar uncovered by the constant winds stands near a large snowdrift, several bones scattered at its base.

title: [[Seord Kerwaith, Mountainside]]
description: Little can survive the constant onslaught of the bitter cold winds rushing across the exposed mountainside.  Towering drifts of snow have formed to either side of a small rocky outcropping, providing limited shelter and respite from the elements.  Partially buried in one of the drifts stands a dark stone pillar, perhaps a route marker for a lost trail.  In the distance, shrouded in clouds of blowing snow and ice crystals, the tallest peaks of the range are visible.

A small rocky outcropping with towering drifts of snow to either side provides limited shelter and respite from the elements.  Plummeting temperatures, ferocious winds and swirling clouds of ice particles make the night all the more dangerous.  The distant mountain peaks, once visible, are now lost in the blinding sleet.  A dark stone pillar, lost in night's shadow, lies partially buried in a snow drift by the outcropping.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, west, northwest.

title: [[Seord Kerwaith, Mountainside]]
description: Surrendering long ago to the onslaught of a glacier, the mountain now lies buried beneath an impenetrable blanket of ice.  Frigid winds whip across the glacial surface stirring thousands of small crystals, each tiny shard capable of flaying exposed skin.  Feeble rays of sunlight are useless in dispelling the unyielding bitter cold.

Surrendering long ago to the onslaught of a glacier, the mountain now lays buried beneath an impenetrable blanket of ice.  The inky blackness of night serves only to compound the ferocity of the frigid winds whipping across the glacial surface.  Thousands of tiny shards of ice, each like a miniature weapon, are capable of flaying exposed skin.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest.

title: [[Seord Kerwaith, Mountainside]]
description: Covered in a perpetual winter, the high mountainside has proven to be inhospitable to all but the hardiest of explorers.  Frigid temperatures, constant winds and sudden snowstorms are all part of the daily experience in this region.  Perhaps, in some distant past, this mountain range was exposed to warmer temperatures and seasonal changes, though only the spirit of the mountain knows.  A solitary dark stone pillar stands in resolute silence.

Covered in perpetual winter, the high mountainside has proven to be inhospitable to all but the hardiest of explorers.  Bitter night temperatures, howling winds and blinding snowstorms serve only to disorient.  The cold-hearted night welcomes the unwary in its embrace, comforting the lost with chill arms as they die upon the mountain.  A solitary stone pillar stands in resolute silence.
paths: Obvious paths: east, southeast, south, southwest, west.

title: [[Seord Kerwaith, Mountainside]]
description: Blinding, swirling clouds of ice crystals further compromise the already treacherous footing on the slippery, glacial ice.  A deep crevasse gives rise to concern for one's safety in this region, as only incredible stresses could cause such a fracture.  Leaning drunkenly, a dark stone pillar stands silent watch over the snow field.

title: [[Seord Kerwaith, Mountainside]]
description: Crashing against the mountainside has caused the ancient glacier to become broken and shattered.  Crevasses crisscross the glacier, their icy blue hues deepening with their distance below the surface.  Gigantic shards of ice, thrust up from the depths of the glacier, twist as they reach for the sky.  Toppled and lying on its side, a dark stone pillar has proven no match against the forces of nature.
paths: Obvious paths: north, south, southwest, west, northwest.

title: [[Seord Kerwaith, Mountainside]]
description: Blue-tinged monoliths rise from the shattered glacial plain, a result of the relentlessly slow grinding process of ice against stone.  An insidious pattern of crevasses and trenches lies buried beneath a blanket of snow, their presence betrayed only by slight depressions.  Occasionally the great ice field is wracked by violent tremors as the mountain surrenders to the tremendous weight and pressure of the frozen river.  A dark stone pillar stands in solitude on the desolate plain.

Rising from the shattered glacial plain, monolithic shards of ice reach into the night sky.  Lying beneath a blanket of snow, an insidious pattern of crevasses and trenches has been created by the relentlessly slow grinding process of ice against stone.  Occasional tremors, violent by their sudden onslaught, wrack the ice field as the mountain surrenders to the tremendous weight and pressure of the frozen river.  Hidden in shadow, a dark stone pillar stands in solitude on the desolate plain.

title: [[Caress-of-the-Moons Manor, Hall]]
description: An unusual copper and bronze sculpture consisting of crescent moon shapes bobs silently at the base of some wide steps.  Surrounding the metal moons on all sides, the walls are covered with a painted depiction of Moon Mages in various stages of stargazing.  The three moons -- Xibar, Katamba and Yavash -- smile down upon the watching mages from their locations high in the painted sky.

title: [[Caress-of-the-Moons Manor, Foyer]]
description: Directly opposite from an ironwood door is a massive portrait of a hunting expedition, though this is far from the only indication of the manor owner's inclinations.  The walls are decorated with an inordinate number of trophies, ranging from snowbeast heads to bearskins and leucro tails.  A snarling boar's head stares down the hall from its perch high above the glazed marble floors.

title: [[Caress-of-the-Moons Manor, Front Yard]]
description: High above, a colorful awning peeks out from the edge of the rooftop between hanging strings of spider vines that cascade down the manor's walls.  At regular intervals along the upper ledges, stone gargoyles leer downward with mouths gaping open, some of their number wrapped in cloaks of vines.  Far closer to the ground, an ironwood door allows entry into the building.

title: [[Caress-of-the-Moons Manor, Side Yard]]
description: Brown and red bricks set into the basalt of the manor outline each of the arched windows and emphasize the building's rich opulence.  Spider vines struggle across some of the sills, winding down toward the ground from their source on the rooftop.  Additional victims of the strangling vines are the gargoyles of varied design that stare from the heights into the gurgling canal.

title: [[Theren Keep, Moat]]
description: A mound of slimy-green refuse coagulates here, providing a shaky foothold and limited view beyond the moat's filthy walls.  The gatehouse looms overhead like a gaping maw, and a narrow ledge leads upwards through a patch of slippery moss.  Brackish water oozes east and west, shallow enough that even a Halfling could wade through without much difficulty.

title: [[Theren Keep, Moat]]
description: A massive catapult stone protrudes from the water like the bald pate of a Gor'Tog giant.  Its unsavory green hue pales in comparison to the blackened mildew that plagues the embattlement, spreading upwards through imperfections in the stonework and fractures left by siege missile fire.

title: [[Theren Keep, Moat]]
description: Frothy white globules erupt from an unknown source beneath the muck and drift slowly in all directions, tainted with grime and residue.  An underwater current sucks them under near a curve in the wall, but they pop right up with stubborn buoyancy.

title: [[Theren Keep, Moat]]
description: Standing well over twice the height of a Human, the moat's stone walls muffle all sounds except the faint trickle of water.  The mildewed waterlines reflect the barony's decline and seep lower with each passing year, falling into decay and corruption like the wizard-kings of the Seven Crown Empire.

title: [[Theren Keep, Moat]]
description: Thriving stoneworts nestle amongst hardened lime deposits against the wall, their whorly stalks striving forth in defiance of the brackish water.  Intermittent splashes disturb the silence, and darkness blankets the channel which curves around the southeastern edge of the Keep.

title: [[Theren Keep, Moat]]
description: A nearly imperceptible current flows from north to south, bringing with it a nagging infestation of hungry mosquitos.  Bobbing along the surface, a discarded chamberpot teeters to one side, revealing a dark, foul-looking liquid.

title: [[Theren Keep, Moat]]
description: Thick vines entangle this portion of the keep, from the topmost parapet to the murky waters swirling afoot.  The long, twisted tendrils obscure the stonework completely, gathering at the waterline where striders and beetles skitter between the leaves.  Oddly, the temperature seems somewhat cooler in this location.

title: [[Theren Keep, Moat]]
description: The moat halts abruptly, obstructed by remnants of what was once the northeast Keep.  Even from this poor vantage point, the devastation is frightening.  The northeast tower lies sideways across the moat, as if uprooted from the ground by a wrathful god and abandoned like a child's toy.  Undoubtedly, no conventional army wrought this awful destruction.

title: [[Theren Keep, Moat]]
description: A luminescent gel-like substance coats the stone embattlement along its roughly-hewn face, pulsing softly with an eerie glow.  The mass tapers off southward, but appears much more prevalent northward where garbage chokes the passageway to just a few feet.

title: [[Theren Keep, Moat]]
description: Discarded rubble, lumber and common trash compose a daunting heap to the northeast, blocking the moat entirely in that direction.  The combination of filthy garbage and stagnant water elevates the stench here to heights no mortal should ever experience, and the narrow, slime-ridden passage southwards looks like it offers little, if any, relief.

title: [[Theren Keep, Rubble]]
description: Broken masonry and trash clog the moat at this junction, forming a makeshift dam that prevents stagnant water from spoiling the northern Keep.  The upper ramparts stand in ruin, clearly the source of all the rubble, but still high enough to thwart intruders despite its dilapidated condition.  Unlike the dank, water-logged channel southwards, the moat looks dry and solid to the east.

title: [[Theren Keep, Dry Moat]]
description: Long iron spikes line the moat's bottom, spaced far enough apart that a nimble thief could walk between them, but sure to impale any fool falling from above.  Gazing upwards, a dark tower pierces the nighttime sky, soft torchlight flickering from its windows.

title: [[Theren Keep, Dry Moat]]
description: The moat descends through a gap in the foundation, the site of a massive cave-in where attackers undermined the castle's embattlements.  Ramparts once thought impenetrable lie about in shambles, blocking further progress beyond the exposed mining tunnel.

title: [[Theren Keep, Mining Tunnel]]
description: Crumbling stone slabs rise from the earth like misshapen gravemarkers, lamenting their downfall from what was once a mighty bastion.  Other fragments choke the very mining tunnel that induced their ruin, as a final act of defiance in a war the descendants of long-dead soldiers can't even recall.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Roughly carved stone walls meet the hand cut blocks of the keep's outer wall to the south.  Moisture creeps down the tunnel walls to gather in a pool on the floor and begin its journey deeper into into the darkess.  An opening, half-heartedly covered up, appears to have led out at one time but is now sealed.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Light seeps through small holes in the ceiling of the tunnel and reflects dimly off the stone walls.  Thin rivulets of water trickle along the rough passage floor, flowing slowly to the north.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Broken strands of cobwebs lifted by an almost imperceptible current of air brush against mildewed walls.  A splintered oak door hangs precariously against the inner wall of a tunnel that splits to the east.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: An oak door hangs in ruins against the stone wall, held in place by one twisted iron hinge.  A collection of rubble has been piled up against the tunnel wall to form what looks like a battle barricade.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Although not visible in the darkness, a steady dripping can be heard as water makes its way from the ceiling to the floor.  A slippery slime covers the floor, requiring each step to be made with caution.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: A few weapons and armor lie on the floor, rust and decay being a testament to the years that have passed since they were last used in a battle.  A garrison banner, still attached to its staff, lies buried under rubble and mud.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Brewer's vats and barrels reveal the past purpose of this room.  Crossbeams still support the pulleys once used to move barrels from the racks to transportation carts.  Tired and frayed ropes hang from the crossbeams, dangling just out of reach.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Empty burlap sacks, long ago robbed of their grain by the smaller vermin that run these tunnels, lay rotting in the moisture of the floor.  The storage racks where the bags were once stored are now little more than splinters tossed about recklessly.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: A caved-in section of the ceiling allows light and air to enter this section of the tunnel.  Sporadic patches of moss growing along the stone walls glisten with moisture in the dim illumination.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Any movement to the east would require stepping on an odd looking slab of rock embedded in the floor of this passage.  A large tapestry depicting a battle of archers versus horsemen hangs on the wall of the tunnel.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Any movement to the west would require stepping on an odd looking slab embedded in the floor of the tunnel.  A large tapestry depicting a scene from a battle hangs on the wall.  A soft glow of light winds its way down the tunnel from the eastern end.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: High in the ceiling, troughs have been carved and a low burning fire finds residence there.  Obviously fed by some type of fuel, the light makes it very easy to see in what would normally be a pitch dark area.  Interestingly, there is a small opening in the lower portion of the north wall.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: To the northeast is the view of a richly decorated room that is quite out of place in these deep, dank tunnels reeking of wet soil and stone.  A glow of light filters through the iron door but reveals only darkness on the other side.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Time and abandonment have not destroyed the beauty of the lavish tapestries and thick carpets that adorn this underground room.  Designed to be self contained, the room contains a four poster bed, a pair of well cushioned chairs, a dining table and a polished mahogany dresser.  A bookcase large enough to hold several month's worth of reading material stands empty against the furthest wall of the room.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Gravel and rock piled about the floor almost hide the expensive tile laid on beneath the rubble.  A shredded tapestry hanging on the wall makes a feable attempt to hide a hole carved out of the rock near the floor.  Studying the tapestry for any indication of what it might have depicted in its better days, your eyes follow it to the ceiling where you notice another hole that is definitely out of reach.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Old meat kegs, now empty, fill this room.  Still present on the stone floor is the salt that was once used to pack the meat.  Now dirty and caked, the salt has managed to keep the room completely dry which in turn has made this part of the tunnels one of the few areas without a mildew smell.  In a divot carved into the wall, sits a wooden box.  A hole, about three feet off the floor, has been bored in the stone wall.  The tunnel continues to the east but gets very low.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: A low ceiling makes standing impossible in this section of the tunnel and the sharp edged stones of the roughly chipped passage makes crawling particularly uncomfortable.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Sticky cobwebs cling to everything that passes through this tight space.  Faintly glowing patches of lichen provide the only source of natural light.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: You find you must twist and turn your body to to maneuver through here.  There will be no turning around at this point, you must ever continue forward or back your way out.  So close are the walls that you can feel the heat of your own breath.  The cold stone is almost welcome as sweat drips from your brow.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Any effort to stand in this portion of the tunnel would be futile.  Movement further north will require a bit of twisting and turning.  The passage to the south, just a few squirms away, appears to be a little more spacious.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Several bones and skulls lie scattered about the floor along with remnants of armor and weapons.  A fire to the northeast has scorched the walls about half way into this section of the tunnel.  White streaks of ash reveal something was drug across the floor and to the south.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: A fire raged in this room at some time in the past.  A fire hot enough to turn the surrounding rock to a molten slag now cooled to glassy smoothness.  A few inches of grey ash on the floor is all that remains of whatever objects were once contained here.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Faint tracks of white ash run from the north and into a hole in the east wall.  A make-shift iron plate which once covered the small opening is now pryed up and allows entry.  Occasionally a slight whisp of fresh air floats in from the south cooling your face just briefly.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Cobwebs trail from shelf to box to rotting bag in this underground storage room. Several old chairs are stacked against one wall, and a pile of splintered crates blocks a portion of the exit to the north.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: This portion of the tunnel has been converted into a storage area for the furniture of the keep that no longer has a home.  A good size hole now covered by a tapestry at one time must have provided access to the keep itself but it is now sealed.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: An old single hole privy fills the majority of this room.  A mirror frame with no mirror inside hangs crookedly on the wall.  Stone and pebbles are piled about the floor making it difficult to find a comfortable place to stand.  A large gaping hole in the ceiling is well out of reach.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Dim light seeping through the gloom from the south provides a welcome alternative to navigating through these dark, web-riddled passages by touch.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Weblike threads dangle in artistic patterns from the ceiling and walls.  The scent of dust, trapped in the sticky strands, hangs heavy in the air.  To the south an arch, now bricked up, silently tells of a time when this passage was part of the Keep's floorplan.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: The rough stone walls of the tunnel are covered with a sticky substance that would seem to be spider's silk, were it not so inordinately thick and heavy.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Ants seem to have taken up housekeeping in this part of the tunnel.  As they crawl about and over your hands you can't help but wonder how they could build a nest in what appears to be almost solid rock.  Light makes its way across the stone floor from a low opening to the west where the area on the other side offers an opportunity to stand and stretch.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: As you move through this tunnel your mind pauses to reflect on the workers that dug it.  Just moving through them is difficult, the thought of having to chisel and pick inch by inch and then haul the debris out boggles the imagination.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: Your knees ache with the pain of supporting the weight of you and all your gear.  Your clothing and other items snag on the razor-like edges created through the impact of metal picks on hard stone.  The passage sweeps from a northern darkness into a western darkness.

title: [[The Breech Tunnels]]
description: As you crawl along this passage, sharp rocks and gravel give way beneath your hands making it difficult to stay on all fours.  The low ceiling traps your breath and makes it hard to breathe, as you fight the sweat that runs off your brow and into your eyes.

title: [[Theren Keep, Basement]]
description: Bricks, shovels, lime and mortar are piled near a bench with other mason's tools, and a stack of smoothly-cut blocks eclipses the basement's rusticated facade.  Additional space opens to the south, and a crude stairway climbs upward on dimpled steps which look like a blind man attacked them with a pick.

title: [[Theren Keep, Sloping Tunnel]]
description: Distorted sounds echo down this pock-marked tunnel, carried on a frigid draft whipping around your legs like a disgruntled poltergeist.  Flickering torches maintain a somber light as the passage descends sharply to the west.

title: [[Theren Keep, Dungeon]]
description: Chilling darkness permeates the chamber despite a glowing firepit, churning sparks like a mage's bungled spell.  A long wooden rack replete with chains and manacles awaits traitorous thieves or murderers, and heavy tongs, branding irons, and leather whips round out the torturer's modest collection.

title: [[Theren Keep, Basement]]
description: This end of the basement remains bare of supplies, excluding a dusty barrel tethered against the wall.  A trail of footprints marches back and forth between a storeroom door and a sturdy ladder, but seems loath to proceed north any further than necessary.

title: [[Theren Keep, Storeroom]]
description: Sealed crates and pallets cram the room from floor to ceiling, most marked as one sundry item or another.  From lumber to furs to perfume, you can bet it's here if traders find it worth the journey to Riverhaven.

title: [[Theren Keep, Storeroom]]
description: Multiple levels of shelves expand the storage capacity here at least twofold, accommodating a stockpile of iron rations which could probably support the keep beyond a thirty-day siege.  Casks of low-grade wine settle in a far corner, as tasteless now as they'd be in a hundred years.

title: [[Theren Keep, Buttery]]
description: Deft craftsmen have fitted massive blocks of new stone, rebuilt cabinets, and added several shelves to these kitchens.  Only faint smudges of indelible black and mild bubbling at the edges of some of the old masonry show that these kitchens were anything other than pristine.  Large kegs of ale and tapped barrels of wine now line the eastern and northern walls.  Pitchers and ladles hang from long brass hooks, and the wide shelves are crammed with preserves and bottles.

title: [[Theren Keep, Kitchen]]
description: If the victuals taste as good as they smell, the current Baron follows his predecessor's tradition and keeps a lavish table.  Fresh fruits and vegetables garnish shelves along the wall, and strings of garlic, dried peppers and sausage dangle from handy hooks overhead.  A scarred cutting board proudly displays an array of dishes ranging from poultry to exotic seafood imported from the Eastern Seaboard.  Each dish bears the hallmark of the chef's culinary brilliance.

title: [[Theren Keep, Pantry]]
description: Barely large enough to accommodate the deobar table and matching cabinets for which it was built, this modest room serves as a staging area for elaborate feasts before their presentation.  Southwards, master chefs prepare renowned culinary recipes foretold by the mouth-watering aromas wafting from that direction.

title: [[Theren Keep, Great Hall]]
description: Seven columns span the chamber in a vast semi-circle of burnished black marble, the middle three curving around a broad dais while the outer pairs brace high, spectacular balconies.  Striking blue-gold banners and silken tapestries proclaim the royal colors of Therengia, but these minor ornaments pale before the tiled dome ceiling and a massive, seven-sided table which dominates the great hall.

title: [[Theren Keep, Gallery]]
description: Voices and laughter echo throughout the gallery, originating from a granite archway and the keep's central hall beyond.  A majestic standard hangs upon the wall in plain view, so that all who enter or exit the Baron's court shall know who it is that offers them hearth and hospitality.

title: [[Theren Keep, Gallery]]
description: A row of evenly spaced torches burns brightly to illuminate the way along this long gallery that stretches to the east.  A large tarpaulin, nailed to the wall, has replaced the old tapestries.  Blue-marbled tiles lead southward through a well-lit entry hall.

title: [[Theren Keep, Entry Hall]]
description: Twin rows of gleaming plate armor stand along the lengthy hallway, resplendent in shimmering surcoats of blue and gold.  A heavy wooden beam protrudes from a nearby pedestal, placed so that it won't disrupt the pristine view, but still close at hand should the entrance need to be barred.  The polished marble floor radiates a soft, blue luminescence as it ripples northward into flickering shadows, like moonlight on the open water.

title: [[Theren Keep, Gallery]]
description: The corridor halts before a drystone wall, recently constructed in a manner unlike that of the surrounding masonry.  A broken shovel litters the ground, quite out of place considering the rich tapestries and extravagant weapon displays to either side.  Southwards, a crude stairway leads down to the lower levels.

title: [[Theren Keep, Garderobe]]
description: Nothing more than a recess in the exterior wall, the latrine's cleanliness speaks well of the servants who attend it.  Sweet-scented jasmine mollifies the air, and a bucket of wash water stands prepared to flush out the chute.

title: [[Theren Keep, Servant's Quarters]]
description: Modest but comfortable, the servants enjoy excellent quarters considering the restricted capacity of the keep.  Woven rush mats blanket the cold floor, and soft bedding comforts the hand-picked personal staff who retire here after toiling in the yards or kitchen.

title: [[Theren Keep, Dais]]
description: A few steps or so above the polished marble deck, this raised platform nevertheless grants a commanding presence over the great hall.  Glowing braziers flank the Baron's throne, infiltrating the chamber with feeble, reddish light and the pungent smell of burning herbs.  Gazing downwards, the hall seems barren and quiet despite its restoration, mourning the ancestral knights, ladies, battle songs, and ballads that echoed through the keep so long ago.

title: [[Theren Keep, Corridor]]
description: Spanning roughly ten feet across, this dim corridor ranges southward to a guard's antechamber.  Thousands of opaque tiles form a vivid mural illustrating the keep before it was razed, silhouetted against a clear blue sky and the rising sun.

title: [[Theren Keep, Ward]]
description: Light and heavy crossbows hang from a convenient rack, each weapon accompanied with a score of deadly quarrels.  A simple table and chair are the only other furniture in this spartan guard post, yielding to a lengthy corridor northwards.

title: [[Theren Keep, Garrison Hall]]
description: This expansive bay accommodates a score of professional soldiers, though ample space remains for twice that number if needs be.  Judging from the perfectly aligned cots and footlockers, the Captain of the Guard keeps his charges orderly and well-disciplined -- even mattresses reserved for infrequent mercenaries lay neatly in the corner.

title: [[Theren Keep, Armory]]
description: Greatswords, battle axes and maces join an immense inventory of weapons staged around the room, and elaborate suits of plate and chain await champions bold enough to don them in Theren's name.  Somehow, a small writing desk littered with scrolls and ledgers squeezes midst the armaments, where a scribe reluctantly logs every piece of equipment.

title: [[Theren Keep, Forge Shop]]
description: This cramped alcove is packed with the raw supplies necessary for the ardous task of smithing.  A single torch casts a dim, flickering light on the different metals, causing faint reflective wisps to dance in an ever-shifting pattern upon the dark granite walls.  A bored Dwarven attendant sits off in a corner in front of a stained and torn velvet curtain.  From somewhere down below comes the faint sound of the pounding of metal.

title: [[Second Floor, Hallway]]
description: Thin moonlight strays through a rough, cross-shaped arrow loop, betraying a flurry of dust stirred up by your movements.  A sturdy oak door leads out to the parapet, and a spiral staircase winds downward to the first floor.

title: [[Second Floor, Hallway]]
description: Dull, featureless stone marks this interminable hallway, and a glimpse in either direction promises little if nothing better.  A flight of short steps ascends to the keep's upper echelons, straining half the corridor's length just to reach the next floor.

title: [[Theren Keep, Hall of Knights]]
description: Heads, horns and furs from beasts both mundane and monstrous decorate the freshly-painted walls of the Hall of Knights, where the Baron's warriors congregate when not feasting in the Great Hall or sparring in the courtyard.  The castellan's office looms beyond an acanth table strewn with local maps and games of strategy, and the keep's chapel lingers to the east like a dull afterthought.

title: [[Theren Keep, Chapel]]
description: Tapered candles provide a warm light for the Chapel of Chadatru despite the dark of night.  Even in the dim light the stained glass window can be viewed.  A richly embroidered tapestry serves as a backdrop to a polished ash altar carved with the image of a golden lion upon its surface.  Oak benches have been placed here so the devout can come and observe the first rays of dawn blaze into existence across the face of the window and cast its fiery light across the altar of the god of justice.

title: [[Theren Keep, Parapet]]
description: This particular corner of the parapet sulks below the northwest tower, rising overhead with all the majesty of an emperor's palace compared to the outer ramparts.  Unlike the weathered stone deck, the tower shows signs of half-hearted maintenance where mud and grime was scraped away by either reluctant servants or guards caught sleeping at their post.

title: [[Theren Keep, Parapet]]
description: The sound of boots striking stone echoes across the parapet whether you step or stand still.  Perhaps a despondent ghost or lone watchman, the source remains obscure though a clear line of sight bares the passageway in both directions.

title: [[Theren Keep, Drum-Tower]]
description: Disjointed boarding provides a makeshift roof over this squat drum-tower, the ancient wood half-charred to a brittle crisp.  Safeguarding the entrance and western courtyard, the embattlement provides fields of fire ranging beyond the outer ramparts, and machicolations to hinder assailants below.  If not for the keep's warlike implications, the picturesque view of the surrounding countryside might even be considered romantic.

title: [[Theren Keep, Parapet]]
description: A tiny bird's nest rests between two square-cut merlons, protected by a wooden shutter still dangling from a few arrow-riven splinters.  Almost laughable in this place of war, the nest's owner has gathered shreds of hay, cloth and fletching to build its new home, now an old souvenir of long-dead men and forgotten battles.

title: [[Theren Keep, Ruined Parapet]]
description: Ages ago, the parapet encircled the northeast tower and continued south to protect the vulnerable flanks.  But now the walkway greets empty space where the tower once stood, its pitiful remnants strewn across the landscape a thousand times over by unfathomable powers.  Even time takes its toll in the aftermath, slowly eating away the weakened embattlements year after year.

title: [[Third Floor, Hallway]]
description: Colorful frescos beautify the walls with bright pastels and soft earthtones, quelling the drab ambience of a stairwell angling down to the second floor.  An assortment of gold and indigo curtains introduces a broad balcony to the east, overlooking the great hall but largely concealed from the occupants below.

title: [[Third Floor, Hallway]]
description: The southwest tower harbors a solid, steel-bound door, bolted shut with broad bands of metal.  Its dark grey fixtures pulse in and out of shadow as if suffused with a restless spirit, foregoing the Starry Road to fulfill a tragic life.  Eastwards, the hallway ventures through the infamous guest quarter, while blithe embellishments illuminate the north.

title: [[Third Floor, Guest Hall]]
description: A fine oil painting distinguishes the quaint foyer to one of several apartments reserved for honored guests.  Despite slender arrow loops housed in the embattlement, the trappings here look every bit as comfortable as the finest inn in Riverhaven.

title: [[Third Floor, Hallway]]
description: The passageway halts before a reinforced ironwood door with elaborate figures etched around the frame.  Faint scuffmarks blemish the door's threshold, and a stout lock ensures the northwest tower remains offlimits to all but the Baron himself.

title: [[Third Floor, Guest Hall]]
description: The scent of recently painted wood lingers where a restored architrave has replaced a severely damaged doorway.  The sturdy door is made of carved deobar, graced with a shiny, new brass doorknob.  Fresh rush matting muffles every footstep ensuring that guests are not disturbed as bustling servants go about their daily chores.

title: [[Third Floor, Guest Hall]]
description: Woven rush matting cushions your footsteps as the hallway veers past the southeast tower and west beyond the common guest suites.  Framed paintings of charming pastoral scenes line the walls and a fine porcelain vase, complete with fresh flowers stands on a marble pedestal.

title: [[Third Floor, Hallway]]
description: A side balcony to the west provides a lofty perch for spying on the great hall, visible through a tasseled silk curtain fluttering from a burnished brass rod.  The sconces along the wall remain empty for one reason or another, throwing the walkway into near darkness.

title: [[Third Floor, Barricade]]
description: Sturdy wooden planks nailed across the northern wall of this room block off all access to the ruined Northeast tower.  A large tarpaulin stretches across the wooden barricade to keep the worst of the wind and moisture out.

title: [[Third Floor, East Balcony]]
description: The damp of the stone wall is somewhat mollified by the vivid tapestries that grace this balcony.  The flickering light of a single torch sheds a pool of feeble light onto the gleaming mahogany deck.  A handsome banister gleams with freshly applied polish, the smooth lines of its curved posts testifying to its newness.  Down below, the hall thrives with newfound effervescence.

title: [[Southeast Tower, Loft]]
description: Sunlight filters through panes of shimmering crystalline glass, spanning the entire roof of this secluded loft.  A sloping bedframe swept with layered down comforters provides guests with a luxuriant cradle for romantic diversions or a simple hideaway to enjoy the pristine skyward view.

title: [[Southeast Tower, Royal Guest Suite]]
description: More queen's parlor than baron's guest chamber, this comfortable apartment could kindle a romantic spark between the most frigid couple.  Rich blue-gold curtains frame a shuttered window, and an exquisite sandalwood dresser offers sumptuous edibles fresh from the kitchen.  Lush floral carpets shroud the stone floor embellished with soft pink rose petals, while a comfy loft lounges below a skylight of crystalline glass polished to a breathtaking sheen.

title: [[Theren Keep, Guest Chamber]]
description: Smelling of lavender and polish, this room bears the hallmarks of refurbishment -- fresh paint and obviously new furniture.  The four-poster bed is resplendent with satin covers, plump pillows, freshly laundered bed linen, and small petal-filled muslin satchels tied with a silk ribbon.  An elegant high-backed chair stands in one corner next to a small glass case.  A candelabrum with tall candles stands on a glossy cabinet with brass hinges and handles.

title: [[Theren Keep, Guest Chamber]]
description: More honeymoon suite than common guest room, the romantic ambience tantalizes your senses.  Freshly laden herbs cover the floor, their sweet scent mingled with jasmine and lavender, and a cozy fireplace contributes to the heady aroma, crackling at the foot of a large canopied bed.  Soft satin pillows shimmer in the light, awaiting their lover's embrace.

title: [[Third Floor, West Balcony]]
description: This elegant balcony stands midway between the tiled ceiling and marble floor of the great hall.  Seasoned mahogany enhances the decor with its deep, reddish brown hue, and luxurious chairs offer the hospitality one would anticipate in a prince's theatre, much less a stone-walled keep.  Nestled in shadow, you have an excellent view of the hall below.

title: [[Southwest Tower, Castellan's Office]]
description: Everything in this room speaks of a sharp, well-organized mind.  Not a yard of floor space goes unoccupied, and the castellan wastes no effort on frivolous artwork or tapestries.  Instead, books and ledgers line the shelves, all neatly aligned according to size, and a wide desk bears a detailed floor plan of the Keep.

title: [[Theren Keep, Garderobe]]
description: The knights enjoy a private latrine reserved for their use.  Fresh herbs are scattered about the floor that give up their scent when crushed underfoot.  Bundles of straw lay handy and a half-filled wooden bucket of water stands to one side of some overturned chamber pots.  While the narrow chute has been scrubbed as far as is possible, the rest is mercifully obstructed from view.

title: [[Southeast Tower, Aumbry]]
description: Once used as a storage place for ceremonial vessels, the aumbry now serves as a home for rats and other vermin.  Dusty cobwebs flutter in every corner, anchored by dessicated husks of spider's prey, and in a few instances, the spiders themselves.

title: [[Theren Keep, Chapel]]
description: Sunlight is welcomed into the Chapel of Chadatru by the rainbow colors of a stained glass window set in the eastern wall.  A richly embroidered tapestry serves as a backdrop to a polished ash altar carved with the image of a golden lion upon its surface.  Simple oak benches have been placed here so the devout can come and observe the first rays of dawn blaze into existence across the face of the window, casting its fiery light across the altar of the god of justice.

title: [[Second Floor, Barricade]]
description: Sturdy wooden planks nailed across the northern wall of this room block off all access to the ruined Northeast tower.  A large tarpaulin stretches across the wooden barricade to keep the worst of the wind and moisture out.

title: [[Theren Keep, Forebuilding]]
description: At first glance, this chamber appears quite innocuous.  Grey stone steps lead down to the courtyard, and huge, black walnut doors welcome guests like lethargic watchmen.  However, machicolations disguised as lion's gullets and cleverly concealed murder holes reaffirm this stronghold shall always be prepared to defend itself.

title: [[Theren Keep, Entrance]]
description: A squat drum-tower overlooks the forebuilding, warding the entrance with ruthless crossbow fire from arrow loops along its battle-scarred walls.  Ascending through engraved marble arches, a series of chiseled stone steps leads into the Baron's resurging stronghold.

title: [[Theren Keep, Bailey]]
description: The persistent sounds of hooves clomping on solid earth and of neighing signals the presence of the Baron's stables.  A deep-rutted path leads north through patches of dry grass, and a small tower hovers to the east, guarding the stone entryway.

title: [[Theren Keep, Bailey]]
description: An aging heavy catapult lies abandoned at this junction in the courtyard, with only a broad, wooden frame and broken crossbeam to distinguish it as a siege engine.  A junk pile near the outer rampart reveals the splintered catapult arm and its water-logged skeins, useless now, but at one time capable of raining death far beyond the barony's walls in the form of massive boulders or fiery concoctions.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, southeast, northwest.

title: [[Theren Keep, Gatehouse]]
description: Buttressed towers stand to either side, housing the drawbridge mechanisms and a half-raised portcullis rusted in place from years of disuse.  The main keep looms to the north beyond an open courtyard, stretching northwest toward some exterior buildings and east where a small grove of trees brightens the landscape.

title: [[Theren Keep, Bailey]]
description: While the walls of Theren Keep bear telltale scars of siege and war, a newly-constructed ballista assumes the charge of her inner defenses.  Skeins of twisted cord notch the weapon's deadly ammunition -- a half score of long, razor-sharp arrows aimed southward should the mighty gatehouse fall to attackers.  A tall wooden rack contains more lethal shafts beside a crumpled tarpaulin, used to protect the ballista during inclement weather.

title: [[Theren Keep, Bailey]]
description: The dirt trail gradually turns to mud as it passes a small shed protruding from the western parapet, and a tall, fractured rampart lingers to the north, opposing the parapet's even crenellations with jagged edges that bruise the daytime sky.  Towards the east caravan tracks lead to the Trader stables.

title: [[Theren Keep, Caravan Stables]]
description: Not a single horse graces the empty stables -- no saddle or harness hangs upon the wall.  If chargers or warhorses ever paced these dusty grounds, they are long gone with the stalwart knights who bridled them.

title: [[Theren Keep, Bailey]]
description: The outer wall runs diagonally from the northwest parapet, turning southward as it skirts the main courtyard.  Here, the upper rampart has fallen into complete ruin -- first weakened by enemy bombardment, then broken off in the final assault and toppled into the moat.  In spite of the damage, a rickety wooden ladder still leans against the crumbling wall-walk.

title: [[Theren Keep, Sicle Grove]]
description: Lush grass and tiny wildflowers blanket the ground beneath a small grove of sicle trees, offering a pleasant diversion from the stark backdrop of Theren Keep.  A well-branched young sicle tree is securely rooted beside an old gnarled stump, a symbolic motion by the Baron and his garrison to reestablish the honorable name of Theren and restore the keep to its former glory.

title: [[Lasa Morit Livery, Stable Yard]]
description: A slight haze of red dust coats the split rails of the small paddock connecting a long thatch-roofed stable to a squat red brick office.  Standing in the shadow of a lone tree, a small herd of horses of varying shade and size patiently whisk away flies with their tails.  One battle-hardened horse remains alone near the water trough, stomping imperiously as he glances repeatedly toward the gate.

title: [[Theren Keep, Storage Shed]]
description: Boxes, crates and barrels of all sizes line the walls from corner to corner midst a thick layer of dust and unsightly rat droppings.  An uprooted floorboard reveals a possible underground passage, but the opening is far too small for even a Halfling.

title: [[Theren Keep, Ruined Wall-Walk]]
description: Crumbled stone shifts underfoot with granulated mortar, but the rampart's sheer width makes it safe enough that a drunken bard would have trouble slipping over the side.  An awful stench rises from below, and glancing into the moat you'd guess this is where most of the Keep's refuse is discarded.

title: [[Boar Clan, Overgrown Path]]
description: Lurking underfoot, the remains of a gravel path lie below sprawling weeds and uncut grass.  A few wooden pikes, their shafts rotting and soft from years of neglect, border the route, still managing to direct pedestrians to and from the field beyond.  Wind rustling the leaves in the nearby forest sounds eerily like the breathy cheers of a faraway crowd of enthusiastic togball fans.

title: [[Boar Clan, Overgrown Path]]
description: A tall hedgerow blocks the view of the field to the west of the path.  Once neatly maintained, the shrubbery reflects the general sloppiness of the winding, weed-strewn walkway.  Discarded like yesterday's newssheet, a torn pennant left near a large wooden pike shifts gently with every footfall upon the unkempt grass.

title: [[Boar Clan, Overgrown Path]]
description: An overturned barrel separates the gravelly route from the large field on the western side.  Trash mingles with the grass and bushes as if the group were lifelong friends, inseparable from birth.  It's not hard to imagine a bustling throng navigating the path on the busiest of days despite the current state of affairs.

title: [[Boar Clan, Overgrown Path]]
description: Hunched astride a bend in the road, a dilapidated wooden shed creaks and groans with every gust of wind.  The curmudgeonly structure looms like an unwanted eavesdropper, interrupting the natural greenery and imposing its dark presence.  While its gravel dies near the shack's entrance, the pebbled path resumes its course to the southwest, retreating to the more welcoming grasses.

title: [[Boar Clan, Overgrown Path]]
description: Scraggly branches protrude from the bulky hedgerow to the south like a centipede's legs.  The shrubbery crowds the path somewhat, but the tall, flowery grasses along the northern edge balance the scene.  A rut divides the rocky path in an uneven line, likely caused by a wheelbarrow's habitual journey.

title: [[Boar Clan, Overgrown Path]]
description: Shattered and askew beside the road, a rotting oaken plank slowly succumbs to the torture of both time and nature.  Deteriorating food scraps and empty bottles abound near a barrel tipped on its side, a gooey sludge leaking from the mouth like regurgitated bile.  All signs point to this area formerly housing the field's concession stand, particularly the faded banner labeled 'SNAX' in faint red paint.

title: [[Boar Clan, Weedy Clearing]]
description: Quite literally, this is the end of the road.  The gravel fades into rugged brush grasses and spindly saplings, likely taking root in more recent years when constant activity in the area ceased.  Surrounded by log fencing, a small patch of land is sectioned off to the west, a crumbling stone well visible through the shafts.

title: [[Boar Clan, Abandoned Utility Shed]]
description: Next to the door, a remarkably intact wooden sign shows a curious but effective stick figure of a large biped wiping its feet on a mat.  Two walls are lined with hooks and cubbyholes, where togballers and the grounds crew could store their muddy gear.  Tattered bits of once-bright clothing and rotted muddy boots still remain, although the main occupants of the compartments now are a few weasels and a surly raccoon.

title: [[Boar Clan, Abandoned Utility Shed]]
description: Racks along the wall contain implements for the care and upkeep of the field.  Rusty rakes, shovels and the like stand at wobbly attention, but a few have fallen out of formation -- especially those where the wooden handles have completely given up the ghost.  Some bins in one corner may have held grass seed meant to fill in divots and bare spots on the field after a round of mayhem, although there is no real evidence of this, and they may have actually held turnips or rum for all the observer can tell.

title: [[Boar Clan, Abandoned Utility Shed]]
description: A ring of rusted keys still sitting on a peg on the wall hints that this may have been the guard room for Togs posted to watch the togballs penned in the adjacent room.  The remains of a table with three collapsed legs and several oversized broken chairs, none of which are still functional, lie in a jumble in the middle of the floor.  Indicative of the seriousness with which guard duty was taken, a pair of dented iron tankards completes the decor.

title: [[Boar Clan, Abandoned Utility Shed]]
description: The roots of an immense tree have broken through the floor here, bringing with them a host of mosses, lichens and fungi.  As a result, the footing is tricky, requiring one to high-step, duck and be wary of slipping.  It is not immediately obvious what this room was used for, but whatever the case, nature has surely claimed it back.

title: [[Boar Clan, Abandoned Utility Shed]]
description: The shattered remains of a door frame along with some badly tilting shelving indicate that this small nook was probably a closet of some sort.  Splintered chunks of wood, most of it liberally gnawed, cover the floor.  Piled on the shelves and slipped off onto the ground nearby, shreds of jerseys lie as if they were still freshly washed and awaiting the next match.

title: [[Boar Clan, Abandoned Utility Shed]]
description: Tattered banners hang from the rafters.  On some one can still see the figure of a boar's head; others are merely limp shreds of fabric.  Little else distinguishes this area other than a fallen length of roof lying atop a fractured skull.  The skull appears too small to be an adult Gor'Tog's, but aside from that, there are no clues as to its origin.

title: [[Boar Clan, Abandoned Utility Shed]]
description: A badly decayed woven rush mat covers nearly the entire floor here.  This must have been the practice room, where players could try out their moves with only a modest number of broken bones and smashed heads.  Lying askew in one corner, a large skull grins as if proud that it remains intact.

title: [[Boar Clan, Abandoned Utility Shed]]
description: Battered wooden crates and barrels are scattered throughout the area, creating a sort of obstacle course to walk through for any but small animals.  It seems likely that they once held foodstuffs, but anything that remained has long since decomposed.  The occasional chittering and the faint scrape of claws suggest that some critters have indeed made this place home.

title: [[Boar Clan, Abandoned Utility Shed]]
description: This appears to be the remains of a large pen.  Rusted, cross-hatched wire presumably once kept unfortunates assigned to be togballs inside, although given that the balls were frequently smarter than their jailers, it's debatable whether they really stayed inside for very long.  A flimsy door swings on one intact hinge, but it is now unnecessary due to wide gaps in the old wire.

title: [[Boar Clan, Derelict Togball Field]]
description: Once lush and verdant, the thick grass sprawls unchecked along the ground.  The massive hedgerows loom over this corner of the field to create an abundance of shadows for all sorts of creepy crawlies to seek for shelter.  Most of the soil is intact here due to the relatively infrequent use during game days, though a giant felled tree creates an imposing dent.

title: [[Boar Clan, Derelict Togball Field]]
description: Trash accumulates upon the ground in staggered clumps, blown onto the grass by errant winds or simply discarded by careless spectators of the past.  The corners of a few benches tossed onto the field jut through the tangle of brambles slowly invading the area.  Sticky mud underfoot emits immodest sucking sounds as people and creatures traverse the turf.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast, south.

title: [[Boar Clan, Derelict Togball Field]]
description: Dense thicket grasses make a play to claim a pair of overturned benches strewn sideways on the ground.  Whether the bleachers were ripped from the sidelines by a terrible storm or a pack of rabid fans remains a mystery, though both scenarios are equally as likely.  Whatever the reason, the long wooden seats inhibit passage westward, but other trailblazers' footsteps and weapons have cleared the brush in other directions.

title: [[Boar Clan, Derelict Togball Field]]
description: Years of abandonment transformed the field's southeast corner into a marshy swamp.  Stagnant liquid refuses to absorb into the water table underground, and since the grassy floor descends slightly, the earth degrades into muck and filth.  Splatters of mud cake the surrounding hedgerows as if out of spite.

title: [[Boar Clan, Derelict Togball Field]]
description: Two dilapidated posts lie willy-nilly upon the ground.  Once designating the brown side's goal, the rotting shafts serve no more purpose now than to give termites and fungi a place to call home.  Debris in the form of jagged branches and decaying leaves restricts passage through the field where there formerly was open space.
paths: Obvious paths: north, south, southwest, west.

title: [[Svesinek Cels, Quiet Forest]]
description: From this high point it is possible to see quite a distance out over the grasslands that slope westward, while to the east a mystical quiet radiates from the forest cloaked in its dark finery.  A plume of smoke drifts over a distant hill, possibly from an unseen chimney.

title: [[Emmiline's Cottage, Kitchen]]
description: A tidy kitchen with whitewashed cabinets and a round oak table opens just beyond a short hall leading from the front of the house.  The scent of chocolate drifts in the air and a kettle of tea burbles over the fire.  Placed neatly near the fireplace is a green cushion with lumps and strands of fur in its cloth.  An occasional breeze moves curtains made of yellow gingham tied off with lace ribbon scraps that hang at the windows.  The table is set for company, and a plaque hangs on the wooden door.

The room is lit only by the lanterns down the hall in the shop area, casting odd shadows across the kitchen that nearly hide the closed bedroom door.  The fireplace is banked for the night, the kettle set on a granite stone in the ash to keep the contents warm for any late night guests.  Kitchen chairs are tucked neatly in their places next to the table, and the cushion in the corner looks lumpy, as if it has been pushed and pulled for hours.

title: [[Onsuwayo's Clinic, Roof Garden]]
description: An oasis of green in a city of barren stone and rock, this garden holds a concentrated subset of the many herbs and plants needed to refresh the working Empath.  Built by a master, the small space mimics a wild environment, with plants growing in a seeming haphazard fashion amongst their natural brethren.  Tall plantings hide the view of the town and mitigate the chill, damp sea winds.

title: [[Onsuwayo's Clinic, Empath's Lounge]]
description: Set on the roof of the clinic, this comfortable room is meant as a retreat for the staff and for visiting Healers.  One side opens out onto a small but well-tended roof garden where many herbs and useful plants are grown.  Inside, several comfortable chairs and sofas await the weary and work-worn.

title: [[Onsuwayo's Clinic, Dispensary]]
description: Moans, groans, screams and the keening of still-conscious beings undergoing excruciating pain and terror emanate from three treatment rooms that open off this rotunda.  The air is cold and heavy with nervous tension overlaid with the stench of blood and the sharp, astringent odors of medicines.  Several coldly efficient S'Kra direct the entire facility, dispensing minor first aid, directing people to treatment rooms and arranging supplies for the harried surgeons.

title: [[Reshalia Trade Road, Farmland]]
description: Just to the northeast the road is rutted, with an obvious track passing crosswise over it.  This is where the farmers usually cross with wagons of refuse, and take their pigs to feed on the daaknuts, often in depressingly large herds.  Depressing for any travellers caught on the wrong side of the stream of porcine livestock, that is.  The farmers are doubtless quite happy with the fertility of their pigs.

title: [[Refreshment Stand]]
description: This crude little stand has been here for some time, judging by the weathering of the wood from which it's built.  Essentially a large table with a few boards nailed up on beams overhead to provide some shade from the sun or protection from the rain, it doesn't look as though it would get much business, but it's a favorite gathering place of the area and the three children behind the table grin as they hand over mugs of ale and rolls of bread and whatever else they might have today.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Grand Approach]]
description: The grand avenue that leads to the Palace is set with elaborate topiaries in the shape of mythical sea-creatures and stately coral formations.  Even the path here glistens like the sea-bed.  Well-manicured lawns sweep away to right and left, surrounding the edifice with a deep green carpet.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Avenue of the Heroes]]
description: Two lines of statues of famous personages and mythical heroes line a wide carriageway made of crushed stone.  Each statue is twice life-size and formed with cunning skill, so that at any moment, they might step down off their pedestals and join the throngs around the palace.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Concourse]]
description: A sweeping carriage drive runs up to the very base of a magnificent stairway carved of white stone.  Day and night, grooms stand ready to assist the nobility in alighting and caring for their horses, while sullen guards stand ready to deal with anyone who causes problems.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Portico]]
description: A wide, sweeping stair of gleaming white alabaster carries the eye from the grandeur of the Palace grounds to the equally imposing portico.  Giant guards flank the doors, immobile as if cast from stone.  The portico itself spreads across the front of the palace offering cool shade from the heat of the day.  Several fountains spout from bronze grotesques set into the wall, their streams running down into stone basins where the traveler may quench a thirst or lave dusty feet.

title: [[Sshoi-Sson Palace, West Portico]]
description: The western portico looks out across the city and ocean to the far horizon.  When the weather is right, spectacular sunsets can be watched from the comfort of stone benches conveniently placed to enhance the view.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Eastern Portico]]
description: Gazing out across the city towards the sunrise, the eastern portico offers an inspiring view to the early risers of the town.  From time to time, services are held here to welcome the day.  A low altar with a sunrise carved into the pale yellow stone is set here for that mission.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Grand Foyer]]
description: The roof rises far overhead to disappear in a glorious chandelier made of hundreds of rows of polished crystals in the shape of fanciful sea-creatures.  The floor is a tesseract of cleverly interlocking tiles of sea-foam green stone alternating with pale alabaster shapes that together form endless rows of breaking waves.  To one side, a hallway leads to the public offices accessible to everyone.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Public Library]]
description: Stained glass in the colors of the ocean is set into crescent-shaped windows high overhead.  Bright light falls on the hushed rows of shelving holding fine matching leather-bound books with embossed gold lettering on the spines.  Dark walnut tables with matching chairs provide places for readers to sit and spread out their research materials.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Provincial Bank Foyer]]
description: Understated elegance is the theme of this, the premier bank of the province.  Carpet thicker than the bedding in many a cheap hostel muffles every sound.  A golden light filters down from giant lamps set with stained-glass, while a gentle perfume scents the air.  Deep banquettes, upholstered in richly embroidered fabrics provide a comfortable resting place for those waiting to conduct business.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Grand Provincial Bank, Bursarium]]
description: Quiet elegance is the theme here, that and the sort of luxury only huge piles of money can buy.  Thick carpet, rare fireflame-patterned silverwood paneling, polished stone counters and trim emphasize the common theme of material wealth and lots of it.  Elegantly liveried tellers quietly handle each transaction with a minimum of fuss and delay.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Public Hallway]]
description: Stark white walls and plain grey stone leech all feelings of warmth from the hallway.  Unlike the grand ceremonial parts of the palace, this area is purely functional with no accommodation made for luxuries for the citizenry who must attend to legal matters here.  Offices extend along the hall and are open to assist even those who keep late hours.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Anteroom]]
description: This is quite obviously a waiting room for some high-ranked official's office.  Dark wood paneling covers the the thick stone walls and the furniture, though sparse, is of heavy construction.  A door set with brass studs leads into the inner sanctum while an iron-bound door that would do credit to a bank leads to the hallway outside.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Office of the Exchequer]]
description: Two features dominate the room: a massive safe big enough to hold a Gor'Tog and a desk easily large enough to serve as a small cottage for a pair of Halflings.  The windowless room's only decor is a pair of silk hangings that depict banking scenes.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Narrow Corridor]]
description: Stark white walls and dull grey stone floor tiles suck any vestige of warmth from the very air.  Grim-faced folk pass by in both directions, and from behind heavily barred doors comes the sound of clinking coins and the scratching sound of quill on parchment with the staccato clicking of an abacus adding a disjointed rhythm to the sounds, not unlike dry bones clacking in some bizarre parody of a dance.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Debtor's Hall]]
description: There is a sense of repressed tension and anxiety in the air.  For all the rich decor, this room seems cold and spare.  A few people huddle along a hard narrow bench along the far wall.  A circular counter surrounds several bored-looking clerks who seem to be engaged in almost any activity other than helping those pathetic few who approach them from time to time.

title: [[Sshoi-sson Palace, Public Hallway]]
description: The plain but serviceable decor extends along this part of the hallway with not so much as a picture on the wall to distract busy citizens as they go about their day.  A hastily thrown-up barrier prevents further travel down the hall to the south, but the offices all seem open for business.

title: [[Emmiline's Cottage, Bedroom]]
description: Dominating the tiny room, a large mahogany four-poster bed stands against the wall, nearly blocking the door from swinging open fully.  A homemade quilt is folded neatly at the end of the bed, the bright red and yellow prints contrasting with the darker reddish brown of the wood.  In one corner sits a table, dwarfed by the oversized bed.  A small wooden chair crowds in another corner, an embroidered shawl draped over the back.

title: [[MAMAS Company, Ratha Branch]]
description: Small, dark, and dust-filled, the room is lit only by one ceiling-hung lantern that seems not to have been cleaned in some time.  Piles of rocks lie scattered in corners and on the scratched and stained counter, sorted by color or weight, or in some cases, by whim.  A frayed map is mounted on the wall behind a hanging set of curiously dust-free scales.

title: [[Mother Magpie's Gems and Metals]]
description: A thin film of grease and dust vies with the cobwebs to cover the floor and counter in the tiny shop.  Old Mother Magpie is a familiar character to residents of the area commonly known as 'Tog Town.  Dealing in gems and precious metals, rumor has it she also sponsors a band of street rats who bring her some of her... rarer items.

title: [[Office of the Malk'smo]]
description: A gaethzen stand-lamp hovers over the large walnut desk which divides the constable's area from the rest of the room.  A rich carpet covers the polished granite floor, but only behind the desk.  A gold plated door leads to the holding cell where the Malk'smo entertain their more serious visitors.

title: [[Shard, Smuggler's Bridge]]
description: Calls from the guards above echo down to a narrow strip of sand beneath the soaring walls of Shard.  The river laps quietly at this beach, marked heavily by footprints leading right into the water.  The prints head toward a sandbar rising barely above the surface about fifty feet out.

title: [[Shard, Smuggler's Bridge]]
description: The river flows by on all sides of this narrow sandbar.  A number of footprints lead west, pointing across the water to a narrow beach beneath the walls of Shard.  To the east, a row of stone pilings rises a few feet above the water's surface, with the nearest one not far away.

title: [[Shard, Smuggler's Bridge]]
description: Wide stone pilings sunk into the water look like they might have been placed there for a bridge which was never built.  Now they provide a precarious walkway across the river beyond the town walls.  The pilings stop about fifty feet from the far shore, but from here you can just make out a narrow sandbar that should indicate a place to ford the last stretch.

title: [[Kygar's Pub, Common Room]]
description: Long tables lined with matching benches fill the roomy pub, standing over a sawdust-covered floor swept clean every day.  Bunches of drying herbs hanging from rafters add spicy scents that mingle with the aromas of meats roasting on spits and the freshly-popped corn kernels that fill wooden bowls.  A small stage has been set up in one corner for minstrels, storytellers and other entertainers.  Contrasting shouts of glee and groans of dismay come from rooms set off to the east and the west.

title: [[Kygar's Pub, Courtyard]]
description: Feathery ferns and seasonal flowers grow abundantly in beds that circle the courtyard, surrounding numerous tables, each with its own canvas umbrella to shelter customers from inclement weather.  A half dozen tall torchieres are imbedded in the ground giving off light and warmth.  Bowls of crunchy popped corn, a longtime tradition of Kygar's Pub, sit on each table.

title: [[Ratha, Greater Cobra Road]]
description: Curious spires of rock, whether native to the spot or carved by some forgotten artist, form a bottleneck to the busy streams of traffic flowing up and down the roadway.  Over the years, passersby have carved names, initials and colorful (and sometimes off-color) slogans on every aspect of the rocks.

title: [[The Raven's Mask and Leatherworks, Sales Room]]
description: Display cases holding leather armor and masks fill much of this tiny shop, but one corner is set up as a comfortable nook beside the stove.  An overstuffed chair sits beside the fire, occupied by a brightly garbed young Halfling man.  The noise of a hammer on metal may be heard from the nearby work room, along with an occasional muffled curse.

title: [[Dennats Baya]]
description: Black laquered cabinets line the walls of the shop, their open fronts displaying an assortment of hair care items ranging from razors to combs.  A small catalog rests on a marble counter that stretches from one end of the room to another.  Tiny iron smoke pots, perched on brass tripods in the corners, are giving off a strong odor from the incense burning within.

title: [[Sisters-in-Lore, Herbal and Alchemical Supplies]]
description: A fire crackles merrily in a cast iron stove mounted in an alcove along the rear wall of the shop.  The remaining walls are covered with shelves lined with colorful glass bottles and vials.  Dozens of cloth bags hang from hooks attached to the rafters, each of which gives off a distinctive fragrance.  Two elderly S'Kra Mur women dressed in identical enveloping black robes potter about the shop, occupied with their daily routine.

title: [[Lower Bank of Ratha, Portico]]
description: The massive slate roof of the bank overhangs the wide entrance, forming a deep pool of shade relieved by a pair of bronze and crystal flambeaux half again as tall as an Elothean.  A quartet of well-armed guards lean on wicked-looking tridents, while their cold ophidian eyes watch every person carefully.  The doors are open to the night and the energetic sounds of commerce waft out from within.

The massive slate roof of the bank overhangs the wide entrance, forming a welcome pool of shade on hot days.  A pair of well-armed guards lean on wicked-looking tridents, while cold ophidian eyes watch every person carefully.

title: [[Lower Bank of Ratha, Atrium]]
description: A wide expanse of cool sea-foam green marble stretches across this noble room.  Far overhead, crystal panes set within a spidery framework of gilded wrought iron provide ample light that in daytime, will flood the room with brightness.  Lofty arches on three sides lead to the various banking departments:  The Bursar for foreign currency exchange, the Cashiers for regular banking transactions and the Bourse for private sales.

title: [[Lower Bank of Ratha, Currency Exchange]]
description: The soft jingle of coins mixes with the sharp "click" of an abacus being rapidly worked.  A low counter separates customers from the moneychangers and a brisk business ensues at all hours.  Cool efficiency suffuses each transaction and there is little or no exchange of courtesies or bonhomie beyond the minimum necesary to complete the task at hand.

title: [[Lower Bank of Ratha, Cashier]]
description: Pale buff marble walls frame an equally bland beige counter where cold-eyed tellers process transactions with a plentitude of speed and accuracy but a notable lack of warmth or attempts at false friendship common to other such institutions.  Business is the order of the day and that which interferes has no place in these cool and efficient chambers of commerce.

title: [[Lower Bank of Ratha, Auction Bourse]]
description: This large room has been set aside by the bank for those wishing to do business among themselves and to prevent the regular transactions from being disrupted.  Heavy velvet drapes line the walls and a thick carpet covers the normally bare marble floor to muffle the sound of buying and selling and the not-infrequent disputes that arise over same.

title: [[Ratha, Well-Manicured Lawn]]
description: Flowers line the thick, green grass.  A small opening between the flowers provides access to the lawn from the street.  A pleasant breeze stirs the flowers, while bees industriously fly from flower to flower.  The feel of the grass between one's toes brings people trickling in throughout the day.

The darkened street surrounds this grassy area.  The flowers wait patiently in the dark for the sun's arrival, while the cool grass slowly stands up straight, preparing itself for the feet of the people who will surely be here with the sun.

title: [[Paedraig's Pawn]]
description: Cracked glass doors block access to the cluttered shelves which line the walls of the shop.  A thin film of oily dirt covers everything in the room, leaving a repulsively tacky finish which clings to boots and sandals with each step across the grimy floor.  The burly figure of the owner stands behind the counter, half-hidden by the shadows which fill the area.

title: [[Barbarian Guild, Great Hall]]
description: A musty dampness pervades this cavernous room, and a faint salt breeze flutters down from a gaping hole in the roof where decades of neglect have caused the weathered beams to collapse.  Faint smudges of paint on the peeling plaster walls evidence the prior existence of proud frescoes, but all that now remains is the occasional hint of a sword arm raised in combat, and the grimace of a dying warrior disembodied from his once-glorious likeness.

title: [[Shard, Smuggler's Bridge]]
description: Tall, drooping trees form a protective circle around a tiny cove on the riverbank.  Scorched pits in the sand mark old campfires screened by the trees from the walls of Shard.  The reason for the campsite is obvious -- a row of stone pilings stretches out into the river, providing a way across that avoids the heavily guarded North Gate.

title: [[Antellius' Weapons Training]]
description: The scents of old sweat and dried blood have been worked into the wooden floor of the salle with the passage of time.  Hundreds of students have walked these polished boards, their skills ranging from inept to masterful.  Blademaster Antellius, the school's patron and head teacher, stands in one corner of the room, appraising his students.

title: [[Treetop Perch]]
description: A small platform wedged between two large limbs provides a stable resting place high in the apple tree.  A canopy of leaves blocking out most of the view of the sky and the ground below gives the perch a feeling of privacy.  It is not exactly quiet here, but the bright song of birds and whisper of a breeze passing over verdant green foilage is pleasant and soothing.  The sturdy trunk of the tree has a couple of steps hammered down the side to aid climbing to the ground below.

title: [[Jack Tarr's Rest, Porch]]
description: Traders gather on the porch of the inn, sipping mugs of ale and puffing at carved bone pipes as they discuss their latest successes or bemoan the loss of a venture.  A bench swing rocks back and forth with a creaking noise as the chains rub against the hooks in the ceiling, and a pleasant breeze from the sea carries with it the sharp tang of saltwater.

title: [[World's End Apartments, Abandoned Lot]]
description: Discarded junk fills almost every inch of the space along the adjoining privacy walls.  Makeshift footpaths weave through the garbage for a navigable route, though one might question the rationale considering the repulsive stench.  A short awning hangs over the broken door facilitating access to the building's interior, holes in the canvas revealing glimpses of the sky.

title: [[Jack Tarr's Rest, Front Hall]]
description: The walls of the foyer are covered with stippled whitewashed plaster and polished teak wainscotting.  A brass bell sits atop the front desk.  From the dents and scratches in the metal, it sees much use as patrons demand service from a harried-looking clerk.  A hallway leads east toward the stairs, while sounds of merriment echo from the nearby common room where guests can enjoy a snack or meal at any time of the day.

title: [[Jack Tarr's Rest, Back Hall]]
description: Exposed oak beams, darkened with smoke and age, crisscross the whitewashed plaster ceiling of the hallway.  The scent of fish wafts from the door of the nearby kitchen, where a cook can be heard berating a hapless assistant.  Seascapes and pictures of sailing ships line the walls, while dark oak stairs lead up to the second floor.

title: [[Jack Tarr's Rest, Upstairs Hall]]
description: A narrow table stands at the northern end of the long upstairs hallway.  Above the table, vases filled with creamy white starflowers hang on either side of a painting of the late Josiah "Jack" Tarr.  Black gauze draped above the painting trails down to pool in soft heaps upon the floor.  Nearby, darkened oak stairs spiral down to the first floor.

title: [[Jack Tarr's Rest, Windrunner's Chamber]]
description: A wide brass bed with a lace coverlet and frilly pillows nearly fills the tiny chamber.  Beside the bed, a crystal vase filled with an arrangement of rosebuds stands atop a nightstand.  An intricately woven carpet covers the floor, muffling the sounds from the common room below.

title: [[Jack Tarr's Rest, Wavedancer's Chamber]]
