description: A vibrant floral carpet covers the polished oak floorboards of the tiny chamber.  The colors of the carpet are echoed in the quilted coverlet atop the dark oak sleigh bed.  The quilt, a traditional "storm at sea" pattern, was at one time believed to be a binding spell to protect those it sheltered from Drogor's anger.

title: [[Jack Tarr's Rest, Upstairs Hall]]
description: A red and gold runner covers the dark oak floorboards of the hallway, the colors vivid against the polished wood.  The gilded frames of the paintings which hang on the whitewashed walls gleam dully in the light.  Each painting depicts a ship on which Captain Josiah Tarr had served before his unfortunate death at sea.  A trapdoor in the ceiling leads up to the widow's walk on the top of the inn.

title: [[Tona Kertigen, Entrance Hall]]
description: Tiles of gold and silver-flecked marble line the floor.  A gentle breeze swirls through the room, rustling papers stacked on ebonwood tables.  Carefully watching the bank's customers, a well-armed guard stands beside the paper screen door leading out to the courtyard.

title: [[Tona Kertigen, Deposit Window]]
description: Bright light shines through an opening in the thick paper walls of the building.  A young acolyte of Kertigen sits behind a tall wooden counter, carefully recording the deposits handed to her.  To the west, a moneychanger awaits those in need of his services.

title: [[Tona Kertigen, Exchange]]
description: Sitting behind a dark ebonwood table, a bored-looking Dwarf awaits those in need of a moneychanger's services.  A large board, listing currency exchange rates, is propped on one end of the table.

title: [[Aesry Surlaenis'a, Tanner's Courtyard]]
description: The pungent smell of curing pelts fills the air, coming from several large vats along one wall of the courtyard.  A paper-screen door leads into the furrier's shop.  To the southeast, a crushed shell pathway lies beyond the yard's wooden gate.

title: [[Aesry Surlaenis'a, Egani's Furs]]
description: Dira'ela Egani sits behind a counter piled high with assorted pelts and body parts of the animals which roam the island.  Busy sorting and cataloging the furs, she always has time to speak with an adventurer about purchasing a new hide.  An open screen behind her leads to the leather repair shop run by her husband.

title: [[Aesry Surlaenis'a, Tanning Supplies]]
description: Several small tables support an array of bottles, jars, patterns and leather working tools.  A delicate counter of darkly polished teak runs across most of the room, behind which sits an aging clerk.  Long shelves line the walls behind the counter, stacked with assorted material.

title: [[Aesry Surlaenis'a, Sefu's Repairs]]
description: Racks of leather armor in various stages of repair fill the room.  Sefu himself sits at a long wooden workbench, laboring over a piece of armor for a customer.  Many of his tools, though still sturdy, are worn from years of use.

title: [[Aesry Surlaenis'a, Shoiya's Gems]]
description: Windchimes of delicate crystal hang from the ceiling of this elegant jewelry shop.  Intricate Elothean shesegri are painted in blue, red and green upon the paper walls.  Shoiya stands behind an ebonwood counter topped by mottled marble, running her business with a serene smile.

title: [[Zenastara's Magical Curios]]
description: Plump seating cushions and plain low tables are scattered around the room.  Bronze lamps overhead provide bright illumination for scholars interested in browsing through the merchandise.  Zenastara, the proprietress of the shop, bustles about straightening and dusting, pausing to answer the occasional inquiry.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Shaft]]
description: This is a mine shaft drilled horizontally into the mountainside.  Particularly noticeable is a blue moss that coats most of the ceiling and wall.  The strong smell of a recently deceased animal forces an involuntary wrinkle of your nose.  At one end of the shaft is a narrow crevice.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Crevice]]
description: Rubble and loam cover the ground and all that remains visible in the sparse light filtering through the crevice is a decrepit old ladder with rusted rungs.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: The strange blue moss throws out an eerie light making it possible to see the surroundings.  Water has corroded the ceiling and the walls, but not enough to erode what looks like a set of mysterious markings.  From this point in the tunnel, there is only one possible direction.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: Stalagmites and stalactites reach out trustingly to touch one another.  Helictites high above amaze you with their beauty.  Glowing in the dim light and resting on the floor of the tunnel are sinister formations.  Other than being in awe of the wealth of natural treasures, the predominant sensation is one of cold as the dampness and chill air start to pervade your body.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Streamlet]]
description: Curving walls and dim piles of rock continually hint at hidden alcoves and endless corridors.  Your muscles complain as you endlessly sidestep piles of rocks in the bed of an old streamlet.  Any attempts to speed through this place are prevented by numerous depressions.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Gallery]]
description: This is a gallery with a basin-shaped floor, where channels have been cut into the roof by swirling waters.  In the center stand several broad cone-shaped stalagmites, most of which are supplied by several smaller stalactites.  A huge unnatural pile of rubble stands off to one side.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: Weaving in and out of large blocks of stone, you stumble across an old fire site.  On most of the walls, the dripstone has formed beautiful cascades, resembling either petrified waterfalls or curtains.  To the north are three identical-looking tunnels.
paths: Obvious exits: north, northeast, south, northwest.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Stony Labyrinth]]
description: It is difficult to keep a sense of direction in this stony labyrinth.  Chambers and tunnels open up in every conceivable direction.  The eerie silence is broken only by the crunch of rocks and crystals underfoot.
paths: Obvious exits: north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Stony Labyrinth]]
description: It is difficult to keep a sense of direction in this stony labyrinth.  Chambers and tunnels open up in every conceivable direction.  The eerie silence is broken only by the crunch of rocks and crystals underfoot.  You also see some scattered bones.
paths: Obvious exits: north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Rubble Pile]]
description: Atop this pile are an odd collection of bones and crude tools.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Saverack]]
description: A large dripstone saw-blade is visible on the ceiling.  Caught in the dim glow of the lights recessed in the wall, it resembles two jaws waiting to clamp down on the next unfortunate soul that chooses to pass under them.  The walls glisten with moisture and are cool to the touch.  A slight breeze wafting across your face carries air both cool and fresh.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Frotoft]]
description: Flickering lanterns cast enormous wavering shadows on the pocketed walls.  Despite the frequently placed sconces, the tunnel recedes into nightlike blackness in both directions.  Unknown sounds whispered from all directions cause you to frequently stop and determine their location.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Frotoft]]
description: Several small structures all possessing a similar design are dotted around this area and appear specifically built for dwarves.  Passing by, the architecture appears spartan but functional.
paths: Obvious exits: north, northeast, east, southeast, northwest.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Frotoft]]
description: The damp and the cold of the cavern that you had previously relegated from your thoughts suddenly becomes more noticeable as a violent shiver takes hold of your body.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Frotoft]]
description: Drawn to this location by contagious laughter and hearty singing, you happen upon Forkbeard's Brodger.  Pausing briefly and sniffing the air, smells of home made food and strong ale tempt you to enter.  The possibility of exchanging information and hearing some new rumors also acts as a lure.
paths: Obvious exits: north, northeast, southwest, west, northwest.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Yarso]]
description: A huge stalagmite rises up towards the cavern ceiling, its top disappearing into the darkness.  Dangling loosely from its sides are several thick ropes inviting the would be climber to explore the darkness.  Pitons hammered into the side offer a more challenging climb.
paths: Obvious exits: north, northeast, east, southeast, south, west.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Vinquoy]]
description: More houses are located in this area and with one exception, they share the same spartan functionality that is reflected throughout the entire dwarven community.  A larger home, known locally as Vinquoy Brach, is the dwelling of the chieftain and his wife and is the focus of a great deal of attention.  Two armed dwarven guards, one on either side of the door of the chieftain's home, scrutinize everyone entering and leaving.
paths: Obvious exits: north, northeast, east, south, southwest, west, northwest.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Howan]]
description: Unlike the rest of the cavern, the floor here has been made purposefully smooth in places.  Pikes, shields, lances and other types of weapons have been placed against the large rocks off to one side.  Several dwarves, suited up in armor are stretched out on the floor off to one side.
paths: Obvious exits: northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Harrgy]]
description: Large boulders litter this portion of the cavern, yet it is easy to skirt around most of them.  Off to one side, several boulders have been chiseled, fashioned into seats and placed in a semi-circle.  A larger stone is shaped like a podium, suggesting that this is either a teaching or meeting place.
paths: Obvious exits: east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Frotoft]]
description: On either side of the tunnel to your north are two especially bright lanterns.  The tunnel, regular and smooth, bears all of the hallmarks of traditional dwarven mining.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Frotoft]]
description: Along the east wall, a multitude of glistening milky-white stalagmites rise up in their delicate beauty like rows of candles waiting to be lit.  The whole area possesses a fairy tale quality, providing a multitude of hiding places.  Occasionally you catch a glimpse of a young dwarven face peeking out from between the stalagmites.
paths: Obvious exits: north, southwest, west, northwest.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Frotoft]]
description: Looking closely at the wall, hairline fissures in the rock are noticeable.  It is unclear whether these are recent or several centuries old.  You resolve to ask someone as quickly as possible.  Hewn into the wall of the cavern are several benches inviting the weary person to take the weight off their feet.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Saverack]]
description: Flickering lanterns cast enormous wavering shadows on the pocketed walls, their light slipping off the surface of a smooth boulder that fills one of the many indentations.  Despite the frequently placed sconces, the tunnel recedes into nightlike blackness in both directions.  Unknown sounds whispered from all directions cause you to frequently stop and determine their location.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Saverack]]
description: Heavy encrustation of magnificent flowstone is located in the recesses of the walls along this tunnel.  At every step, strange and beautiful objects sweep into view.  Reddish wormlike growths coated with quartz and glistening crystals of white gypsum dot the ceilings, walls and floor.  Lanterns have been placed in small alcoves at regular distances.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Dunnett]]
description: A small, well lit chamber suddenly comes into view, compelling both humility and silence.  Four vertical monoliths, each owning a corner, buttress the roof.  In the center of the chamber a set of smaller grey stones has been placed in a circle.  The chamber is completely silent, all sounds from the cavern have died away.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Lairorung]]
description: Carefully chiseled into the floor within the circle of stones is the hallowed image of Kertigen.  Unlike other areas of the dwarven settlement, where some of the floors have become worn and smooth with age, the surface here appears unchanged from its original state.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Goi's Pierowall]]
description: An unknown odor makes you sniff as you enter the workshop and it is unclear whether it is originating from the bottles of reagents and solutions on the shelves or the fine dust resembling charcoal that covers the floor.  Colorful crystalline bull's-eyes, crystals and other polished gems have been placed on Goi's display case.  A huge grinding wheel stands off to one corner, surrounded by various other tools used for polishing, sanding and cleaning.  Close to the wheel is a large trough.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Freel Brach]]
description: A thick layer of dust lies on the floor.  This hut awaits a new occupant.

title: [[Lairocott Brach, Muckele's Hoy]]
description: Heat, noise and the smell of sweat assail your senses as you enter this busy workshop.  Hung on one of the walls is an ornate suit of armor, several pick axes, sturdy helmets and other mining accessories.  Muckele Rognvald stands at the forge, fashioning yet another suit of armor.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Entrance]]
description: Gigantic boulders are strewn all over, steep rock faces surround this area and a large hole lies in the ground.  Firmly secured to several of the boulders is a rope ladder.  Other than the sinkhole, there do not appear to be any obvious exits.

wayto.1189: ;e fput 'stow left';fput 'stow right'; move 'climb creeper'; pause; waitrt?

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Ledge]]
description: More shining deposits glitter before your eyes.  Making a mental note of the exact location, you consider returning with the correct tools to mine these rich deposits.  High above shines a faint light, possibly the exit from the mine.  A rope ladder dangles above you.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: More rich veins of ore and crystals in the rock face attract the eye and emphasize the wealth of unmined deposits in this tunnel.  Hanging from the ledge is a rope.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: A large pile of boulders stacked in the passageway and an overturned wheelbarrow force you to edge by the wall and skirt around these obstacles.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: Sturdy timbers at this juncture are in stark contrast to the disrepair that you have witnessed elsewhere.  Similarly the boulders, rocks and pebbles in this room are different.  Although weathering and constant erosion have taken their toll throughout the mine, for some reason this area has been spared.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: A ghastly sight confronts you entering this portion of the mine.  Poised to attack, battle axe in one hand, shield in the other, stands a dwarf frozen in all of his glory.  What he was about to fight or defend himself from or what left him in this sorry state, can only be the subject of conjecture.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: A strong smell of rotting flesh fills the air.  The source appears to be a rodent that met its demise here, its corpse still partially preserved by the cold temperature.  Mounds of crushed rock that do not appear to be the result of mining litter the floor.  A huge natural bridge stands to the south.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: Thin translucent sheets of calcite punctuated by brown streaks hang down from the ceiling.  Unlike most of the mine, there are no timbers that have been used to shore up the roof or walls here.  An eerie, dark silence pervades the gloom.  To the east lies a narrow passageway.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Lair of the Beisswurm]]
description: Walking quietly through the dark slippery passageways is claustrophobic.  Turning a tight corner, you almost bump into a large solid slab of ice which stretches across the entire tunnel and prevents further passage.  Encased in the ice is a huge seemingly perfectly preserved creature.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Bridge]]
description: Standing on the long stone bridge, you take a moment to peer over the sides only to see a deep dark chasm that appears to have no end.  Fighting a brief moment of vertigo, you struggle to steady yourself and catch your breath.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: The light thrown off by the ever present moss is reflected by a myriad of small crystal fragments embedded in the walls of the tunnel and is reminiscent of the nighttime sky.  A huge natural bridge stands to the north.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: The beams that shore up the tunnel have been eaten away in places.  Icicles line the wall and trails of a slimy substance line the tunnel floor.  In the faint glow, the exhalation of your breath momentarily forms a fast dissipating cloud.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: The passageway levels off here allowing you to slow down and catch your breath.  The guiding light is even scarcer causing the occasional stumble, stubbed toe and silent curse.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: Stepping over piles of rock, debris and abandoned tools, the entrance to a wider passageway starts to open up.  The loud reverberating echoes of the crunching sounds made by your footsteps announce your presence.
paths: Obvious exits: north, south, up, down.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: A chill in the air forces a shiver and the realization that the temperature has dropped.  The bluish moss on the ceilings and walls is less abundant which makes it harder to see and forces you to concentrate on your surroundings by using your other senses.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: Small creatures scuttle away at your approach.  Large rocks placed in a semi-circle and remnants of litter suggest that this was an ad hoc eating area.  Overturned metal containers litter the floor.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: Carts still filled with ore, rich veins in the rock face, pick axes and shovels all provide further evidence of a hasty departure by the miners that plied their trade here.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Tunnel]]
description: This long corridor appears to be an old abandoned mining tunnel that runs east to west.  The timbers shoring up the low ceiling are all reminiscent of traditional dwarven mining.  The south wall has a very smooth surface.

title: [[Abandoned Mine, Rock Fall]]
description: The corridor comes to an abrupt end here.  A rock fall has sealed the route, preventing further progress.  The pattern of the rocks suggest that the rock fall was caused purposefully to prevent something from getting out rather than preventing something entering.

title: [[Foothills, Abandoned Road]]
description: The path underfoot is overgrown with weeds and almost completely covered with dried, fallen branches yet still feels surprisingly firm.  A few pine saplings off to one side struggle to push up through the heavy soil.

title: [[Foothills, Abandoned Road]]
description: Meandering rows of saplings impede your progress as the path seems to try to envelop you in foliage.  Glancing northeast to get your bearings you see mountain brush beginning to take over the landscape.  Occasionally, as you trudge along, your feet scuff up bits of dirt and clay.

title: [[Foothills, Abandoned Road]]
description: The rusted remains of an iron wagon, long abandoned by its owner, lay to one side of the path.

title: [[Foothills, Abandoned Road]]
description: The road's never-ending battle to survive the onslaught of the foliage seems to be a losing one at this particularly overgrown stretch.  The rhythmic buzzing of insects serves as a reminder that, to some, this place is home.

title: [[Foothills, Abandoned Road]]
description: A single pine stands, aloof and deserted, like a lone soldier after the battle, forgotten but yet on guard.  Gnarled and twisted roots cling to the poor soil in a desperate grasp, yet this guardian still manages to provide a place for a small nest.  The road widens as it winds to the north.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: The road here is composed of a chocolate-brown clay, cracked and chipped in places where it has dried after a season of heavy rains.  From here it wends its way through hills covered in dry scrub, dropping from sight as it ducks behind a bend in the distance.  To the north rises a range of stony mountains, their heights dominated by one particularly tall, looming crag whose shadow falls heavily upon the lesser hills around it.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: A rockslide of mud and stone almost seems to have brought an entire mountain to its knees a few paces to the west.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: The hard-packed dirt of the road has been broken into a thick layer of loose dust by the passage of many feet and hooves.  An occasional roadside footprint, nearly knee-deep in hardened clay, indicates that mud must be a real problem in times of heavy rain.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: Tree-dotted hillsides rise on both sides of the path, providing ample high ground and cover for would-be attackers.  The road here is mostly flat as it meanders along the valley floor, although there is the slightest incline to the north.  One especially large tree lies fallen near the edge of the road, its roots helplessly exposed.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: The road takes a sharp bend here where it begins to slope more steeply to the west.  The rough hew of the road's northern wall and the beginnings of a dropoff to the southern valley floor indicate that the path here was not created by the simple passing of travellers, but was instead purposely cut into the hillside.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: The hard, brown clay of the road is pitted and rutted where it has been traveled during heavy rains.  Although most of the footprints in the road are from human-like creatures or domesticated animals, there is on occasion a large print of a four-toed creature which appears to have a set of rather pointy claws.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: The path takes a sharp east-northeast turn where it contorts to follow the ridge of the hill above.  The bend offers a fine vantage point for watching the brush-covered valley to the west, far past which can be seen the stony fist of Sorrow's Reach, thrusting angrily into the sky.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: A tall, regal pine stands watch here over a bend in the road formed by the tapered end of a ridgeline stretching off to the east.  The vegetation in the valley below, somewhat dry and brown to the southwest, transitions into a deep green as it nears the valley floor to the north.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: A thick jungle of dry brush covers the hillside bordering the southern edge of the road, while downslope to the north lies an impenetrable mass of vine-laden oaks.  Although the gathering of trees seems somewhat thinner to the east, the dense vegetation makes travel via the road your only real option.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: Tall, moss-covered conifers rub shoulders with lush, green oak on the slopes bordering both sides of the road.  An occasional glimpse through the curtain of trees on the northern downslope reveals the path to be paralleling a river.  To the east you can see a break in the trees where the road turns to march down the hillside below.

title: [[Foothills, Road]]
description: Tall pines stand in silent vigil at a sharp west-north curve in the road.  Steep hills curve protectively above to the south and east, while to the north the landscape drops sharply as it descends to meet the river below.  A slight smell of charred wood hangs upon the air.

title: [[Foothills, Campsite]]
description: Charred branches and the occasional ring of blackened stones indicate that this area is used as a campsite.  The lack of ground vegetation and presence of many footprints in the soil suggest that the grounds are well-frequented.  A wide dirt path runs through the campsite, leading from a steep hill to the south down to the riverbank.

title: [[Foothills, South Riverbank]]
description: A clear blue river flows shallow and wide over a multitude of rounded stones.  On the far bank, a great jumble of earth stretches up to a stone road paralleling the river to the west.  A wide path of hard-packed soil climbs its way uphill towards a small flat area to the south.

title: [[Foothills, South Riverbank]]
description: A small game trail runs here among the clumps of reeds sprouting between the stones along the riverbank.  Majestic trees of pine and oak thrust high overhead from an upslope to the south, providing cover from the elements.  The far bank, by contrast, is a barren, rocky waste of a cliff which stretches from the riverbank up to and beyond a stone road cut into the hillside.

title: [[Foothills, South Canyon Rim]]
description: Tall patches of grass and an occasional clump of reeds grow here among the smooth stones of the riverbank.  A small game trail wends its way among the grasses, trailing from the flats to the east up a small incline running west along the beginnings of the southern canyon rim.

title: [[Foothills, Pine Tree]]
description: Securing a comfortable perch, you survey the vast wilderness below.  A sea of foliage blankets this part of Elanthia to protect it from the ravages of the seasons.  To the south, the road below gasps its final breaths in the distance as it decays into oblivion.  Beside you a nest of pine needles, long grass and scrub brush rests in the arms of its host.  A sudden breeze causes a slight bending of the tree top as it resists yet another force of nature.

title: [[Foothills, Oak Tree]]
description: An ancient oak tree crowns the top of this hill, its wide branches arching high into the heavens to provide shelter for man and beast alike.  Whatever kind soul planted the acorn from which it grew knew much of the magic within the earth, for here all seems a little kinder, a little quieter than whatever may occur on the hillsides below.

title: [[Foothills, Dell's Edge]]
description: A large cut-out of mountain and earth opens up near the southern edge of the dell.  Granite rubble, too small to be of any use to the Dwarves who once worked this old quarry, marks the path through the tree-lined foothills.  Up ahead, the opening to a dark cavern is blocked by a small wooden shack, its rickety door hanging limply from rusted hinges.

title: [[Foothills, Wooded Path]]
description: Cutting through the thick pines, an unkempt path climbs the hill southward at a steep incline, while to the north it descends to a dusty road.  Gnarled, brittle branches reach out at all angles, threatening to grab and trip at any opportunity.  Light filters through skeletal limbs, casting shadows on the ground litter in random patterns that change as the sun moves through the sky.

An unkempt path through the dark pines climbs the hill southward at a steep incline, while to the north it descends to a dusty road.  Skeletal branches reach out like dark hands, threatening to grab and trip at any opportunity.

title: [[Foothills, Wooded Path]]
description: The angle of the path gives travelers a workout, navigating through the trees that thin toward the rise to the south.  Ground litter makes footing treacherous at times as well as noticeably muffling noise underfoot.  Despite the obvious lack of use to the area, the abundant sounds of wildlife indicate it is quite a thriving environment.

The trail rises steeply through the thinning trees to the south, giving travelers a workout heading either direction along the precipitous slope.  Ground litter and the reduced visibility make footing treacherous at best as well as noticeably muffling noise underfoot.  Cricket song fills the air, deafening at times, obscuring the otherwise gentle sounds of nighttime wildlife that might be present.

title: [[Foothills, Wooded Slope]]
description: Pine trees line the slope to the north, heading downhill along a trail to the dry road barely discernable through the trees.  A wide field opens under the daytime sky, where soft grasses sway with the breezes rushing over the open plain.  Soft grasses sway with the breezes rushing over the open plain, a path pressed into the ground leading from the tree line to a meadow in the distance.

title: [[Wildflower Meadow, Before the Gods]]
description: Wildflowers circle a leafy bush and a large, flat boulder, the surface of which is rounded due to years of exposure to the wind and rain.  Lush grass blankets the ground like a living carpet that softens footfalls.  A faint path heads toward the tree line to the north, while the field drops off elsewhere in the other directions.

title: [[Foothills, River]]
description: Icy-cold water flows smoothly past the stones underfoot, adding its whispers to those of the winds blowing up the river canyon which stretches off to the west.  The jumbled mass of a collapsed hillside on the north riverbank provides a stark contrast to the neat, rocky shores of the south.  A fine view of the sheer eastern face of Sorrow's Reach is afforded by the open space of the river.

title: [[Foothills, North Riverbank]]
description: It appears that part of the northern hillside has recently given way, for a large tumble of rocks and splintered trees leads from the riverbank to a small ridge above.  A few steps to the south flow the stony, cold waters of the river.

title: [[Flagstone, Burrow]]
description: Small scraps of cloth, driftwood, and various unidentifiable pieces of jetsam line the walls and floor of this dank, fetid burrow.  A heavy odor almost seems to squeak 'Rodent!' in your nostrils with every reluctant breath you take, and the occasional scrabbling you hear in the recesses of the hole is certainly more than just your imagination.

title: [[Low Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: The road angles steeply here in its cliffside trek through the mountains, making travel an exercise in caution.  Occasional washes of dried mud, the remnants of water runoff from melting snows on the high slopes to the north, dirty the otherwise smooth stones.  Several of the road's mighty flagstones appear to have fallen to the canyon floor below, victims of a long-ago collapse.

title: [[Low Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: A crumbled tower of black stone, pitted along its once smooth face, lies here in a great heap along the southern edge of the road.  Several large, charred timbers jut from the pile like skeletal fingers, pointing at the heavens in mute accusation of a long-ago crime.

title: [[Low Mountains, Cliff Wall]]
description: A wide stone road which stretches off to the east ends here at a sheer cliff wall, giving way to a decrepit wooden bridge that spans southward across a small gap in the canyon.  From the cliff heights far above juts a small promontory of stone, behind which you can see a small cave leading into the mountains.

title: [[Foothills, Stone Road]]
description: The smooth, grey flagstones of a well built road abruptly end here in a massive jumble of stone and broken trees, the remains of a hillside which has tumbled into the river below.  Although there are signs someone has been digging to clear the debris, the only way the road may be traveled for now is to the west.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Entry]]
description: A black granite arch looks out upon the remains of a flagstone road that stretches west towards a tall spire of grey and black rock.  Paired doors carved of solid onyx hang askew on broken hinges to either side of the arch, held upright by the remains of an avalanche recently tumbled down from the nearby hillside.  The road continues through the arch and on into the darkness, with light from the outside dimly illuminating the way in and downward.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Entry Hall]]
description: The smooth, finished walls of this tunnel mark it unmistakeably as a Dwarven clan home.  Small, musty clouds of dust rise at the slightest movement, their presence attesting to the long-ago abandonment of this area by its creators.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Entry Hall]]
description: The spirits of an ancient people mutter softly with the echo of every sound that reverbrates through the tunnel.  To one side of the path lists an abandoned oxcart, its axle rusted and split by long years of neglect.  The highway makes another downward turn to the east and widens into a natural cavern.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Great Hall]]
description: Sparkling gems embedded in the ceiling high above refract torchlight upon the surrounding walls in bizarre, kaleidoscopic patterns.  A starburst constructed of varying shades of marble dominates the center of the chamber floor, its surface curiously clean in stark contrast to the surrounding dust.  Three small passages to the east lead further into the depths of the clan home.
paths: Obvious exits: northeast, east, southeast, west.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Dank Tunnel]]
description: Water trickles from a hairline fracture along one wall, across the floor and under one of the doors lining the tunnel.  A strong smell of decaying vegetation hangs in the air.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Council Chamber]]
description: A long, low table set with several wooden chairs curves before the forward edge of a slightly raised circular dais.  Rotting tapestries hang behind the dais, their colors muted by age and further sullied by the great clouds of dust that kick up with every disturbance of the floor.  A large steel door, covered with lime and streaks of rust, sits in a recess at the back of the chamber.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Dusty Passage]]
description: The passage narrows here, the weight of the hillside seeming to bear down from above.  Several doors are set seamlessly into the surrounding walls, distinguishable only by slight color variations in the stonework.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Dank Tunnel]]
description: The soft burbling of an underground spring whispers from somewhere beyond the tunnel walls.  A long patch of phosphoresecent scarlet fungus climbs one wall of the tunnel, the dim light it emits casting sunset hues upon the doors set into the granite.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Dim Corner]]
description: The light dims considerably at this juncture of the corridors.  A tunnel leading to the east has collapsed into a massive pile of rubble, preventing further passage into the clan's stronghold.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Dusty Passage]]
description: Gaezthen spheres in finely-worked silver sconces line the walls of the corridor at regular intervals.  Vague outlines of doors mark the entrances to private dwellings.

title: [[Abandoned Clan, Buried Treasures]]
description: A collection of finest Dwarven stonework fills this shop, stout furnishings that, while simple, will last several lifetimes.

title: [[Low Mountains, River Bridge]]
description: The bridge on which you stand has definitely seen better days.  Wide as two men are tall and the length of a large, fallen pine, it has dry-rotted from too many years of wet snows and blistering summer suns.  A number of holes in the decomposed floorboards offer glimpses of the river below.

title: [[Low Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: A decrepit, flat wooden bridge crosses the canyon to the north.  The bridge appears to be a hastily assembled substitute for the original stone bridge, the remains of which arch a few feet over the canyon on either side.  A road of wide, grey flagstones winds southwest into the mountains.

title: [[Low Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: The ancient stone road winds ambitiously along the southern face of the mountain range, turning frequently in its effort to bypass obstacles thrown up by the steep, rocky slopes.  Clumps of small stones and the occasional large boulder line the northern edge of the path, silently watching your passage.

title: [[Low Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: At times wide and flat, but most often a steep, winding path, the road here writhes snake-like in its travel through the rocky heights of the mountains.  Much of the road is cloaked in shadow, as what light comes from above is oft blocked by the high, stony crags on either side of the twisting path.

title: [[Low Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: Great peaks of craggy grey stone, devoid of vegetation, rise above on all sides save for a steep, winding road that stumbles its way northeast down the mountain.  The road's builders apparently decided at this point that passage over the mountains was impossible, for here the flagstones enter the gaping black maw of a tunnel.

title: [[Mountains, Tunnel]]
description: A soft glow emanates from the tunnel mouth before you, but the light quickly fades as it filters into the tunnel's malevolent, grasping blackness.  To the west climb the silent, grey flagstones of the ancient road.

title: [[Mountains, Tunnel]]
description: Like a Will-O-Wisp waiting to lure the unwary to their doom, the dim circle of the tunnel exit glows in the distance below.  Your only choices are a heavy eastern descent to freedom, or to trudge into the sucking blackness which lies a steep climb to the west.

title: [[Mountains, Tunnel]]
description: Darkness swirls and eddies about you like a malevolent fog, clutching greedily at your clothing as you feel your way along the ancient road.  The stones underfoot are slick with moisture, and with each scrape of your feet whisper of unseen chasms ahead.

title: [[Mountains, Tunnel]]
description: A faint, glowing circle squats stolidly in the western firmaments above, indicating a steep climb to the freedom of open skies and fresh air.  Other than your erstwhile lunar companion, the darkness here is absolute.

title: [[Mountains, Tunnel]]
description: What faint light manages to filter from the nearby tunnel mouth is quickly absorbed by the hungry blackness all around you.  There is an odd rushing sound, akin to that of strong winds blowing through the tall trees of a forest, coming from outside the tunnel.

title: [[Mountains, Waterfall]]
description: You are on a wide plateau of stone, high above a mighty river gorge which slashes its way east into the distance.  All around you towers the treeless, rocky spire of Sorrow's Reach, its stony roots curving protectively down around the canyon's western limits.  A mighty river of white water bursts eagerly from a cavern mouth high upon the north face of the Reach, roaring forth to plummet into a wide pool in the depths of the canyon below.

title: [[Sorrow's Reach, Cliff Path]]
description: The path here is barely wide enough to accommodate a single person.  The wall to the west offers little in the way of support, being nearly devoid of handgrips and just as slick as the rock below your feet.  One slip of a foot to the east lies a drop into the reaches of infinity.

title: [[Mountains, Waterfall]]
description: A road of square grey flagstones begins here in a corner guarded to the west and north by the sheer cliffs of the Reach.  The assembly of dull grey stones, shiny black where they have been chipped or worn smooth by passing traffic, stretch behind the waterfall to the east before winding their way up the mountainside.

title: [[Mountains, Behind Waterfall]]
description: The great roar of the river beast rushing from above beats upon your ears like a winter storm battering a coastal village.  Although this small stone grotto would at first glance seem an ideal hiding place, its algae slickened floor and body soaking humidity make it unlikely anyone would use it as such.

title: [[Mountains, Waterfall]]
description: A sharp bend in the road provides a good vantage point for monitoring traffic passing near the waterfall to the west.  Several large boulders border either side of the path, providing ample cover for would-be assailants.

title: [[Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: A slight sound of rushing water reaches your ears, complementing the smooth whisper of the winds which blow up the canyon and across the stony face of the Reach.  The road here, level to the northwest, begins to climb slightly as it stretches to the east.

title: [[High Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: A gnarled, twisted pine, bent with age and stunted from a life far above the treeline, hangs precariously over the edge of the canyon rim as if considering an end to its pitiful existence.  Something seems to have taken the signs of the tree's weakness as an invitation to attack, for most of its bark has been shredded away from its trunk in long, thin strips.

title: [[High Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: A sharp bend in the road has been rendered treacherous by the collapse of most of its surface into the canyon below.  Only one width of flagstones remains at the narrowest point, and it appears that a great deal of the earth underneath has already washed away.  Long, sharp scratches in the mountain wall bordering the road almost appear to be the frenzied digging of some creature intent on widening the passage.

title: [[High Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: Tall piles of small, black stones lie on either side of the road here, slowing passage along mountain.  Several of the stones have been used to create a crude fire ring on the uphill side of the piles, and a few animal bones, picked clean of flesh, lie scattered about the area.

title: [[High Mountains, Stone Road]]
description: Weeds choke the cracks between mighty flagstones of coarse grey rock.  The road here rises slightly to the north, while a bend to the southwest begins a torturous descent to the hills below.  A rope bridge can be seen in the distance, stretching across the canyon from a rocky outcropping to the northeast.

title: [[Sorrow's Reach, Cavern Mouth]]
description: You are standing on a massive slab of flat, grey stone cut into one side of the Reach.  The north and west walls are soaring towers of granite, while to the south and east lie sheer cliffs which stretch a lifetime's fall to the canyon floor below.  A rope bridge, attached to a natural outcropping of stone, sways in the breeze above the canyon.

title: [[High Mountains, Rope Bridge]]
description: A sharp, cool wind tugs at your clothing as you stand upon this modest bridge of stick and rope.  Far, far below you can see a small wooden bridge spanning the canyon, and even further beyond stretches a slight band of blue which you can only assume to be the river.

title: [[High Mountains, Rope Bridge]]
description: Ringed by dark clouds of grey, the massive, stony crag of Sorrow's Reach looms above you to the north like the thrusted fist of an angry earth-god.  A deep river gorge has ripped its way through the lands at the base of the Reach, creating a formidable barrier to those who would scale its heights.  The canyon would be nigh impossible to cross, were it not for a simple rope bridge which stretches across to a stone plateau in the mountainside.

title: [[High Mountains, Small Path]]
description: A small footpath wending its way from the north ends here at the top of what must have been a mighty avalanche indeed.  Splintered trees and boulders the size of small houses lie jumbled together in a great rockslide which seems to reach all the way to the foothills below.

title: [[Promado Village, Mountain Pass]]
description: A small trail leading west through a tangled morass of weeds and brambles ends here at a soaring cliff wall, rent open by a narrow crack in its craggy face.

title: [[Promado Village, Middle of Pass]]
description: The pass winds and twists between rugged walls of dark stone, boulders precariously balanced on the cliffs far above.  The numerous craters on the overgrown path, where chunks of rock lie embedded as deep as a foot into the stony soil, bear silent testimony to the danger here.

title: [[Promado Village, Mouth of Pass]]
description: The narrow pass through the mountainside changes shape here, widening into a valley to the west and squeezing into a narrow, rocky passage to the east.  In the shadow of western cliffs stands a ruined village, ramshackle huts and crude wooden buildings standing empty and silent, not even the chirping of birds or the buzzing of insects relieving the eerie, dead stillness.

title: [[Promado Village, Broad Trail]]
description: A broad trail, weeds shooting up though the pebbled road, leads west into the center of the silent village.  The mountain pass stands to the east, and a narrower, less-traveled path runs far to the southwest.

title: [[Promado Village, Village Boundary]]
description: The eastern boundary of the village proper is a tangled mass of dry grass and weed grown between piles of splintered boulders tumbled from the cliff face above.  Tiny abandoned homes, most of them long ago flattened into kindling, lie scattered about the landscape.  The tip of a black obelisk can be seen poking its head over two still-standing homes to the west.

title: [[Promado Village, East Circle]]
description: The eastern trail merges with a wide, circular boulevard here, broken cobblestones littered across upturned black soil.  A tall, black obelisk looms in an open plaza to the west, encircled by the road that arches protectively around it.
paths: Obvious paths: east, southwest, west, northwest.

title: [[Promado Village, North Circle]]
description: North of the village monument, this part of the boulevard runs past a small, ramshackle building with two small obsidian obelisks sitting on its front porch.  A smaller footpath, all that remains of a larger road, wends to the northwest through tall, dry grasses.
paths: Obvious paths: southeast, south, southwest, northwest.

title: [[Promado Village, Northern Lane]]
description: This path leads through a tangle of ruined and fallen huts, the only fragments and reminders of a once prosperous village.  The worn footpath, fresh tracks still evident upon it, curves from the south to the northeast, where it disappears from view behind a ramshackle wooden building.

title: [[Promado Village, West Circle]]
description: The west end of the boulevard runs before the tallest building in the village, a church sided with clapboard and peeling white paint.  Several ruined homes stand in the shadow of the building's tall bell tower.

title: [[Promado Village, South Circle]]
description: South of the village monument, this part of the boulevard passes by the burnt-out shells of sad, empty houses.  A smaller road stretches off to the south.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, south, northwest.

title: [[Promado Village, Obelisk]]
description: A tall obsidian obelisk, chipped and cracked and sunken into the earth at a jagged lean, stands at the center of the village.  Broken and abandoned buildings stand silently around the boulevard, dwarfed by the tall, crumbling facade of a church to the west.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, south, west.

title: [[Promado Village, Southern Lane]]
description: This narrow, overgrown trail winds between rows of collapsed rubble mounds that might once have been homes.  The trail continues southwest, and rejoins the main boulevard to the north.

title: [[Promado Village, Southwestern Lane]]
description: Unlike the utter desolation due east, this street shows slight signs of rebirth cropping from the earth.  Grass patches clump in front of the run-down houses.  Above the squat shacks lining the south side of the road appears a modest-sized knoll, crowned by a building seething with plant growth.

title: [[Promado Village, Small Cottage]]
description: In stark contrast to the rest of this section of the lane, one whitewashed cottage stands snug and whole in the midst of the squalor, proving that is indeed possible to rise against and to conquer adversity.  A deep-grained walnut door, graced with delicate unicorn and panther carvings, acts as entry into the abode.

title: [[Promado Village, Southwestern Lane]]
description: Clumps of daisies peek out of the earth, dwarfed by the remains of burnt buildings lined along the sides of the dirt path.  A lone wooden sign dangles from the remains of one of the houses.

title: [[Promado Village, Knoll]]
description: The dirt road ends at the base of a knoll, changing into a cobblestone path leading up the tiny hill to a thatched-roof house.  Vines choke the whitewashed structure in a tangle of green tendrils.  Stray wildflowers dot the hillside, struggling to create a spot of brightness amongst the remains of the rest of the village.

title: [[Promado Village, End of Southern Lane]]
description: The lane comes to an end at a morass of bramble thickets here, rubble vanishing in the tall, wavering grass.

title: [[Promado Village, Cart Path]]
description: The path cuts through a grassy field, away from the village and towards a cluster of low, grey stones to the southwest.  Deep gouges cut into the ground betray the passage of a heavily laden wagon.

title: [[Promado Village, Graveyard]]
description: Dozens of grey stones, many toppled flat and half-buried in the overgrown grass, lie scattered about the ground.  Although most are faceless, half-legible inscriptions on one or two show them to be gravestones.  The number of markers seems abnormally large for such a small village, and it is apparent from the crowds of newer stones jammed between the neatly ordered rows that many of the graves were dug in a short period of time.

title: [[Promado Village, Outside Cave]]
description: A multitude of smooth grey stones peep above the sea of grass here in the shadow of the cliff wall at the southern end of the valley.  The dark mouth of a cave stands at the trail's end, a pair of deep wagon tracks leading right inside.  A fetid smell drifts from the cave, something like a dead animal rotting.

title: [[Promado Village, Refuse Heap]]
description: The footpath ends behind a large wooden building, where a refuse heap piled high with obsidian chips, broken hammerstones and various other garbage sits in silence.  A long, ash-white bone juts from the bottom of the pile.

title: [[Luscious Lavas]]
description: Large slabs of crudely cut obsidian lie stacked in careful piles along the walls of this oak-paneled workshop.  Small chips of flint-knapped stone litter the floor, ready to slice the feet of the unwary.  A sign on the far wall invites attention.

title: [[Promado Village, Tiny House]]
description: The ancient timbers of this one-room house creak and sway dangerously every time a wind blows through, as if it may collapse upon itself at any moment.  The furniture has disintegrated into wooden shards and scraps of cloth, and the old fireplace is home to a massive spiderweb from which tiny scarlet eyes gleam.

title: [[Promado Village, House on a Knoll]]
description: Queued up like a line in a Carousel, the cobblestones sweep in a broad arc from the bottom to the top of the knoll, ending at a quaint house.  Several snakeweeds grow thickly around its perimeter, their oblong leaves jutting outwards as if to guide visitors away from the chestnut door leading inside.

title: [[Promado Village, Cave Tunnel]]
description: The welcome light of day streams in through the mouth of this dank tunnel where it exits to a small, grassy valley.  Further south, the rough stone floor slopes sharply downward, out of sight and closer to the stench of decay that pervades the gloom.

title: [[Promado Village, Tunnel Bend]]
description: The tunnel levels here from its steep slope to the north and turns sharply to the east.  A pair of wagon tracks end abruptly at this point, their depth in the hard-packed earth suggesting the cart's burden was a very heavy one.

title: [[Promado Village, Dead Pit]]
description: The tunnel ends here at the brink of a vast pit, piled high with the bones of the dead.  A sea of ashen bones and skeletal remains gleams in the dim light, eyeless sockets turned up to the earthen roof as if searching for release.  From far beneath, perhaps at the bottom of the pit, comes a chorus of slithering, clicking noises, like a million wriggling centipedes nesting in the bones.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Gate]]
description: A lofty wall of some oddly colored green metal blocks the view west.  All other directions lead to grim reminders of death and mortality.  A low, creeping vine has taken over much of the open ground, but here and there, broken stumps of stone or metal protrude unevenly.  A bare path made of thousands of tiny, rough pebbles leads northwest towards an irregular, slab-sided chapel.

The darkness of the night is intensified because of the shadowy presence of a high wall which blocks all views to the west.  Creeping vines camouflage any odd protrusions from the ground, making the walk in the darkness a little more treacherous.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Close-Packed Graves]]
description: Numerous rows of grave markers stand side by side in oddly close array.  Most are broken and overturned, but a few still stand upright.  Tiny flowers grow amongst the stones, pale white and delicate.  Their clean, sweet scent seems so out of place in this grim setting that it disturbs rather than uplifts.

The stillness of the night is occassionally broken by the sound of some unknown creature rustling through weeds and vines.  The graves are barely visible in the darkness, their broken remains dark shadows in the night.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Alabaster Fountain]]
description: Surrounded by dozens of tiny grave markers, an elegant alabaster fountain stands, a monument to the silent dead.  Here and there, some of the graves have been disturbed in a curious manner.  The earth has been overturned, as if pushed up from below by some unseen force.  Several tiny caskets lie tumbled about, broken and empty.
The sound of trickling water emanates from the fountain that is barely visible in the dark.  The shadowy silhouette looms against the night like a dark sentinel.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Close-Packed Graves]]
description: Many small gravestones here are ruined and destroyed, perhaps by time and the weather, yet the wreckage seems systematic, as if someone had been searching for something buried.  To the north, a long row of massive and elaborate obelisks and other shapes rise along the high wall of the cemetery.

Dirt lies piled in uneven ridges, the remnants of overturned and unearthed graves scattered throughout the area.  Shadows dance across the path in dark, ominous swirls that seem to mimic the movements of passersby.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Funerary Memorials]]
description: Running along the high wall, many strange, even bizarre stone monuments rise, each striving to outdo the next in elaborate paeans to the forgotten dead rotting beneath.  Many-winged beings raise a pot-bellied figure dressed as a Trader in mute exaltation.  Dying warriors make bloody obeisance to a stoop-shouldered figure clad as a mighty warlord.

The outlines of several stone monuments are barely visible, their shapes and features hidden by the darkness of the night.  The sound of something moving echoes in the gloom, but the source of the disturbance never reveals itself.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Close-packed Graves]]
description: Numerous rows of grave markers stand side by side in oddly close array.  Most are broken and overturned, but a few still stand upright.  Tiny flowers grow amongst the stones, pale white and delicate.  Their clean, sweet scent seems so out of place in this grim setting that it disturbs rather than uplifts.

The stillness of the night is occasionally broken by the sound of some unknown creature rustling through weeds and vines.  The graves are barely visible in the darkness, their broken remains dark shadows in the night.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Funerary Memorials]]
description: Numerous monuments to the dead rise all about, each its own testament to the long forgotten corpses that lie buried beneath.  The wind sighs in a hollow dirge, perhaps in keening tribute to the deceased.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Funerary Memorials]]
description: Northwards, the land falls away rapidly in a sheer drop-off, leaving naught but an echoing vista of open air.  Nearer at hand, one huge monument dominates the garish row of memorials along the high wall, though the heroic figure surmounting the pile of stone seems oddly distorted.  The ground around it is dry and bare of dust and dirt, yet faint marks of something heavily-clawed mar the surface.

The outline of a singular granite figure towers over the rest of the memorials, its details hidden by the blackness of the night.  Muffled sounds, perhaps an animal foraging for food, or perhaps something else entirely, fill the air.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Bare Ground]]
description: The ground here is bare and devoid of all, except for faint marks etched in the stone paving here and there.  The remains of numerous wooden and latticework frames still stand along the edge of the precipice, and in one place, a stone platform juts out over the edge.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Bare Ground]]
description: The ground here is barren and untended.  Oddly, not one piece of grass or one flower grows anywhere.  The walkway is mainly dirt and gravel, the footing at times treacherous.

The crunching of gravel fills the air, though whatever is walking or moving along the ground cannot yet be seen.  An odd rustling noise is carried from nearby, like the sound of some great bird shaking out its feathers in preparation for flight.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Rock Platform]]
description: Tall wooden poles are set in regular groups deep into the stone.  Many bits of bone and other identifiable remains lie scattered about.  The air is heavy with the nearness of death, as though some great power or ritual had once been worked here.  Far off in the sky, a huge black bird glides on motionless wings, rising in slow circles, yet never straying far from this place.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Rocky Ground]]
description: Underfoot, the ground is hard and stony.  No grave or monument rises here, as if the space had been left unused when this place of the dead was abandoned.  Faint lines etched into the rock indicate where monuments might once have been placed.  Nothing grows in the desolation, save one tiny tree that grows in a scant pocket of earth in the cracked stone.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Burial Mounds]]
description: Soft earth rises in low mounds all about.  Some are topped with standing stones, but most are bare or scattered with rubble.  There is a sweet smell of ancient mold and rot seeping into the air.  Scabrous yellow flowers grow among piles of broken rock, and lichen the color of dried blood spatters the stony surfaces.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Burial Mounds]]
description: A series of dark green grassy mounds run along the cemetery wall.  Some seem recently created, an oddity in this place that appears otherwise abandoned, while others appear to have existed for quite some time.  A sense of uneasiness fills the air, perhaps caused by the heavy silence that permeates the area.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Burial Mounds]]
description: Along the high wall protecting this place, many low, mossy burial mounds stand.  Few are marked in any way and fewer still seem intact.  Almost all of them have been dug up, unearthed, or otherwise disturbed.  Whether the desecration took place long ago or more recently is impossible to discern, and there is no hint as to its cause.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, High Mound]]
description: One mound, higher than all the others, looms over the cemetery like an ominous guardian.  The top is crowned with a single massive standing stone of dull black slate.  No grass grows here, yet the earth appears darkly rich.  Faint footprints run across bare loam, and many drag marks criss-cross its surface, yet the silence that reigns over all yields no hint as to the source of the activity.
The eerie outline of the high mound looms against the backdrop of the dark night sky.  Sounds drift from the top of the mound to echo in the night, their source unknown.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Mound Top]]
description: Footing is treacherous here, as loose earth slides with each step.  Bits of bone glint white against the bare dirt, and many broken weapons lie scattered, lost perhaps in some ancient battle.  Slightly to the west stands a dull black slab that rises from the mire in the low center of the mound.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Mound Top]]
description: Here at the top of the mound, the center of Promado Village is seen.  The church steeple is barely discernible, its white clapboard sides almost pristine as it stands next to several abandoned and demolished homes.  The black slate slab stands in the center of the mound, larger than life.  Around the base, someone has arranged rocks and sticks into some oddly-shaped symbols, their meaning long forgotten.
The outline of the village below is barely discernible in the dark of night.  The slab that stands in the center of the mound looms in the darkness, an eerie sentinel against the night sky.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Burial Mounds]]
description: A series of dark green grassy mounds run along the cemetery wall.  Some seem recently created, an oddity in this place that appears otherwise abandoned, while others appear to have existed for quite some time.  A sense of uneasiness fills the air, perhaps caused by the heavy silence that permeates the area.

title: [[Abandoned Cemetery, Burial Mounds]]
description: A series of dark green grassy mounds run along the cemetery wall.  Some seem recently created, an oddity in this place that appears otherwise abandoned, while others appear to have existed for quite some time.  A sense of uneasiness fills the air, perhaps caused by the heavy silence that permeates the area.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Tunal]]
description: A huge granite boulder from Outer Hibarnhvidar leads into this sharply sloping tunnel.  Bricks of red-streaked granite populate the grey stone of the walls, floor, and ceiling more and more until nothing but the granite bricks frame a black iron door at the lower end.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Gatikalar Stof]]
description: Enormous granite blocks, fitted with no visible mortar, create thirty-foot walls and a vaulted ceiling.  Thick veins of ore meet in a whorl in the center of the floor.  In the east wall, a wrought iron keystone twenty-five feet above the floor supports a red granite arch which is flanked by two fifteen-foot-high granite arches, one black and the other grey.  Flames that light the chamber rise from a trough along the top of each wall.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Vigan Stof]]
description: Curving granite blocks form the circular walls for this huge chamber.  Thick veins of brick-red hematite emanate from the wrought iron keystone that supports the arch in the west wall.  Long low benches have been hewn from the granite floor and surround a huge map constructed from fine metals and gemstones that is inlaid into the floor.  A broad set of low stairs leads to a dais to the east.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Tawkisik Stof]]
description: The veins of hematite change to solid iron in the granite blocks nearest the dais.  A raised square of granite holds the Guildleader's seat, and a nearby pedestal holds the Guildleader's tankard.  A table at the rear of the dais holds an oaken hogshead.  Stairs lead down from the dais.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Viikalar Stof]]
description: Bright silver strata flow through the granite blocks, catching the torchlight to illuminate even the far corners.  Training dummies are scattered about, obviously rended and repaired many times, and makeshift weapon racks stand along the north wall.  Stones of various sizes protrude from the floor at different heights, no doubt meant to keep warriors mindful of their footwork.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Tunal]]
description: Dozens of alcoves in this broad corridor keep an arsenal of weapons and armor at the ready.  Torches are set into the wall between each pair of alcoves.  Guild guards keep watch over the alcoves.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Eldar Stof]]
description: Eleven statues of barbarians line the walls, each on one knee and facing the flaming brazier in the center of the chamber.  Triangular stones inlaid in the floor point from the edge of the brazier to the statues honoring it.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Turn Stedh]]
description: Polished granite walls surround a massive iron chain that is sunk into the inlaid marble floor and climbs into the darkness above.  Stairs lead up the north wall around the chain and into the Guildhall's famous tower, and a brushed bronze door is centered on the east wall.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Sarv Stof]]
description: Whorls of copper, malachite, and azurite run from the black granite arch in the northwest corner to the open stone doors in the east wall.  Large racks line the south and west walls.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Kvafelar Stof]]
description: An occasional cry of pain can be heard through the loud laughter echoing around the circular bar that dominates this room.  Stone stools of varying heights surround the bar, and tankards of numerous sizes clutter it.  Midway between matching sets of stone doors to the west and northeast, a set of steps climbs the wall to a raised balcony.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Ram Viikalar]]
description: Stone steps climb the wall from the drinking hall below to this wooden balcony.  Large squared mikkhalbamar timbers are cantilevered from square holes in the stone wall, and thick red oak planks are laid across them.  Simple stools line the stone wall, and two low oak chairs in the center of the balcony face each other across a table set with blocks and handles.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Shal Turn]]
description: Silver runs in veins throughout the walls.  Intricate patterns guide the eye to stairs that continue upward around the walls from the steps below.  Torches are pushed through the large links of an iron chain that hangs through the center of the chamber from high above.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Shal Hrot]]
description: A yard-tall rampart, punctuated with large stone slabs, surrounds two-thirds of the circular area carved from the mountainside.  The jet-black granite of the floor and rampart sets off the smooth grey of the stone slabs.  The architecture amplifies every footstep into an echoing clatter.  Two spears stabbed into the granite mark the sides of an opening to stairs leading down.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Shal Turn]]
description: The platinum spiderweb below gives way to a lace of silver and grey animite that covers every block of this chamber's twelve walls.  The heavy lace embedded in each step and makes the stairs hard to discern from the walls.  A massive iron chain is set into the granite ceiling and torches have been shoved into its links.  The stairs continue around the walls and upward from the steps below.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Shal Turn]]
description: Streaks of gold glitter in the blocks of stone carefully fit together to form the six walls that the stairs continue to spiral around.  The walls smoothly transition from the four walls below into what appears to be eight above.  The massive iron chain, laden with torches, continues above and below.

title: [[Elding Gwilt, Shal Turn]]
description: Eight granite walls are covered with a web of platinum threads inset into the stone.  Stairs, due to their lack of platinum embellishment, can be clearly seen to continue up and around the eight walls.  The platinum glitters in the light from the torches jammed into the iron chain hanging through the center of the chamber.  The torches barely light the steps leading down the tower.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar Trader Guild, The Floor]]
description: This long, wide room appears to be a partially converted brewery, the air still filled with the scent of ale.  Rows of casks line the walls, leaving the center of the floor clear to make room for business.  Clerks, traders and commodity brokers intermingle with local farmers and miners to discuss the ever-changing prices of commodities, while the noisy sound of braying animals can be heard to the east.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar Trader Guild, Office of Interprovincial Trade]]
description: A foil map hangs across the back wall, tinted and textured to show the five provinces of Elanthia.  Other than that single piece of elegance, the room is completely utilitarian with a wooden plank floor and a single desk of neatly stacked paperwork.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar Trader Guild, Stables]]
description: Mountain hardy beasts of all sorts find themselves in neighboring stalls in this slightly cramped but serviceable stable.  Bales of alfalfa and hay have been pushed against the wall, leaving only the bare minimum amount of area needed to lead caravans and carts in and out from the road.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar Trader Guild, Rock Garden]]
description: This long abandoned portion of the brewery has been cleaned up and turned into an exquisite rock garden.  An intentionally meandering path of carefully pieced slate rock connects the stables and cask room, as well as a shiny brass contraption in the western garden.  Old ale casks, cut in half, have been used as picturesque flower boxes, while other pieces of cask have been used as trimming around individual beds nestled within colorful collections of polished stone.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar Trader Guild, Rock Garden]]
description: The dazzling rock garden occupying the wide warehouse portion of this old brewery has been muted by the presence of a lone working still that takes up the western portion of the wall.  Several Dwarven workers tend to the still, oblivious to the beauty of the arrangements of colored rock and crystal around them.  Channels of water run through the garden both to further beautify the area as well as to keep the room at a comfortable temperature.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar Trader Guild, Guild Leader's Office]]
description: The Guildmaster's office has been carefully coordinated to incorporate the vision of a sun rising above the mountains.  Purple and gold silk drapes hang loosely against the stone walls with light from wall sconces peeking through behind it like the first rays of a new morning in a cloudy sky.  A large gold-inlaid rosewood desk glows in the reflected light from the smokeless candles set about the room.  On a small shelf behind the desk rests a crystal decanter and four matching wine glasses.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar Trader Guild, Cask Room]]
description: Damp and cool, this room acts as a tasting room for guests and a break room for clerks, although it is hard to say who is actually doing the most sampling.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar, Orphanage Common Room]]
description: The confines of a low ramshackle building converted to living quarters are furnished haphazardly.  Doors, arch, hallway and alcove branch off from the long squat common room without symmetry, giving the appearance of being tacked on as needed.  A wood stove burns brightly, mismatched benches and chairs pulled in a cluster around it.  Only windows on the street side of the building contribute light or fresh air, and although the room looks frayed and made of collected discards, it is clean and neat.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar, Orphanage Classroom]]
description: A shelf holds writing slates and chalk for lessons, and long backless benches stand arranged in symmetrical rows.  At the far side of the room is a table displaying student efforts.  Of note is a large, chipped ceramic bowl furnished with water, pebbles and turtle.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar, Orphanage Headmaster's Chamber]]
description: The Headmaster's chamber is no more elaborate than any other area of the orphanage.  His battered desk is missing a drawer, and his chair's rungs are reinforced with twine.  A window - a luxury - looks out into the street, and behind a screen is a small cot.  Drawings pinned to the wall only add to the clutter.  Nevertheless, there is a hint of good will in his disorder, that there is too much work for one man, but what is left undone has been put aside for the priority of affection rather than neglect.

title: [[Hibarnhvidar, Orphanage Library]]
description: Tucked in the front corner of the common room, the library bookshelves form two of the walls to divide it as a separate room.  The largest window in the whole orphanage looks out into the street, so during daylight hours it is the brightest lit and cheeriest of nooks.  A comfortable chair is a favorite spot, and its faded cover and squashed cushion suggest many children have retreated here.

title: [[The Three Turnips, Common Room]]
description: A semicircle of lumpy overstuffed chairs faces a roaring fire crackling in a large flagstone hearth set into the rear wall of this spacious chamber.  The remainder of the space is covered by heavily scarred oaken tables, most of them replete with massive frothing tankards and wide platters heaped with the hearty fare favored by Toggish laborers.  Based on the relaxed postures of many of the patrons, it is clear that they consider this their home away from home.

title: [[The Three Turnips, Banquet Hall]]
description: Unlike the atmosphere in the rest of this establishment, there is an air of formality here.  The enormous long table that runs nearly the entire length of the room is draped in white linen, and there are centerpieces of freshly cut flowers at regular intervals.  The chairs are in markedly better repair than those found in the common room.

title: [[The Three Turnips, Taproom]]
description: Several thick-legged stools, braced for the weight of the pub's massive patrons, line the front of a long wooden, slightly warped bar.  On the barkeep's side are stands supporting three large kegs and a shelf filled with a motley array of bottles and jars.  A large rectangular mirror covers most of the back wall, affording drinkers the opportunity to make faces at themselves while they enjoy their libations.

title: [[The Three Turnips, Game Room]]
description: This room has been set aside for 'Togs who wish to divert themselves with something other than mere eating and drinking.  Mounted on the back wall is a well-used two-colored dartboard.  Numerous nicks and gouges beyond the border of the target silently testify to the fact that the contestants are often more enthusiastic than skillful.  A few scattered armchairs are provided for the comfort of those waiting their turns to cause structural damage.

title: [[The Singing Raven, Common Room]]
description: A perpetual haze of tobacco smoke hangs just under the low ceiling, illuminated from beneath by the orange glow of the roaring fire in the flagstone fireplace that takes up most of one wall.  Opposite it, a long bar runs the length of the room.  Rough wooden tables and chairs are scattered about, of wildly varying sizes to accommodate travelers of all races.  Day and night, the room is filled by those stopping for a bite to eat or liquid refreshment.

title: [[The Singing Raven, Upstairs Hall]]
description: A single glass-enclosed lantern on one wall provides the only light on the narrow landing.  The flickering flame inside wavers and gutters, casting moving shadows along the wood-paneled walls.

title: [[The Singing Raven, Peregan Room]]
description: Warm golden highlights glint from the deep brown wood-paneled walls.  An immense four-poster bed dominates the room, covered in thick, clean-smelling down comforters and piles of fluffy pillows.  A small table is placed conveniently close to the bed, holding simple refreshments.

title: [[The Singing Raven, Pine Room]]
description: A faint scent of baking bread drifts through the small room, apparently located somewhere near the kitchens.  The knotty pine paneling's warm yellow hue is matched by the bed coverings on the low, thick mattress.

title: [[Barley Fields, Farmer's Path]]
description: Though the path widens and descends as it curves southwards, the other end crests over a hump of earth and dirt and vanishes.  The identifiable sounds of rural civilization leak over from the other side of the barrier, but all of the muffled noises dance just at the edge of earshot.  All around, waist-high lengths of barley sway gently in the wind.

title: [[Barley Fields]]
description: A simple wooden plow rises from the rippling ocean of barley, contrasting as starkly as would a dark warship in a sea of crystal blue.  Nesting birds have built their homes in the joint where the handles meet the blade.  Even though the farmer has abandoned the plow to the weather, its usefulness shall not end.

title: [[Tzgaa'lakh'adu'gai, Narrow Trace]]
description: Green barley makes a miniature wall to the north as the path fades within the stalks of the waving crop.  Here, at the edge of the fields, the fine topsoil gives way to a stony and pebble-covered surface, the defining line nothing more than a mud-filled irrigation ditch.

title: [[Tzgaa'lakh'adu'gai]]
description: An odd series of rounded stones poke up from the dirt as the trail curves northwards, indicating that this path may have once been used frequently enough to be at least partially paved.  Except for the few stones still clinging to the vestiges of what was once a road, they've all fallen down the side of a steep slope.  Occasionally, one of the smaller stones bounces down the rock slide and vanishes from sight.

title: [[Tzgaa'lakh'adu'gai]]
description: Tattered remnants of faded cloth shiver in the wind but are not pulled from their half-buried locations at the base of a rock slide.  Shifting any of the stones to discover what else may be hidden beneath the stones is naturally discouraged by the frequent crunching of the stones as they shift under the slightest provocation.

title: [[Tzgaa'lakh'adu'gai]]
description: Wind tears across the barren surface of the rocks, changing direction and force often enough to maintain a constant state of turbulent drafts.  A handful of sickly weeds find purchase in what little ash ridden soil the wind has failed to claim, unusually curved from their lives in the overbearing gusts.

title: [[Tzgaa'lakh'adu'gai]]
description: The deep scars of a washout gut the trail across the center, splitting the route into two halves before swallowing it completely.  Bits of black rock and tiny showers of grey dirt patter down the washout's slope, dislodged with every touch of the wind and every stray movement of a landing bird.  The peak of the volcano rises above the swirling wind, completely indifferent to the travelers braving its rocky routes.

title: [[Tzgaa'lakh'adu'gai]]
description: Narrow to the point that it very nearly is non-existent, the trail clings tightly to the side of the volcano's slopes.  Glassy black rocks jut from their perches along either side as though they were hands reaching out to the sky for salvation.  Some of them have received their deliverance, having fallen to new resting places far below.

title: [[Tzgaa'lakh'adu'gai]]
description: All semblence of a proper path have vanished, and only the sharp angles of massive stones embedded in the surface of the volcano guide those who are not of avian descent.
