title: [[Darkmist Moor, Country Church]]
description: A small rustic church, with an overhanging roof and rough-hewn wooden pillars, watches solemnly over the area.  Ivory-white paint is flaking and peeling from its walls, which are embraced by creeping vines of deep green ivy.

title: [[Darkmist Moor, Trail of Bones]]
description: A strange trail of bones is scattered amidst the tall grasses, wending its through the boggy marsh.  The moor's vegetation grows a bit thicker to the east as one travels further from the road.

title: [[Darkmist Moor, Trail of Bones]]
description: Just south of the bone path, the land drops suddenly for several feet.  The earth of the slope has been disturbed in small patches, and several clumps of heather lay scattered and uprooted.
paths: Obvious paths: north, east, southeast, west.

title: [[Darkmist Moor]]
description: The rocky ground is covered with blue-grey lichen and sturdy pale yellow weeds.  Fingers of mist whirl around a broken arrow wedged between two thin ribs of a long decayed torso.  The lower half of the skeleton lies several feet away, likely dragged by scavengers, with a single moldering boot clinging to what little is left of its owner.

title: [[Darkmist Moor]]
description: The dark green grass here is slowly losing its battle with mortality.  Patches of light brown dead grass stand out against the darker green of their surroundings.  To the southeast you can see the silhouette of a dead tree, its now bare branches reaching up as if in supplication.  Several cracked rocks litter the ground, their shattered, blackened surfaces indicating that some power other than weather and time are to blame for their state.

title: [[Darkmist Moor, Trail of Bones]]
description: An ancient stump sits nearly buried in the tall grass of the moor.  Pale grey fans of some unidentifiable fungus spread from its side while specks of a scarlet mold stretch up the trunk from the roots.  In contrast to these tenacious vestiges of life, the bleached trail of bones runs past the stump and stretches to the west and northeast.

title: [[Darkmist Moor]]
description: An uprooted tree lies on its side, surrounded by broken branches and pieces of bark.  A patch of blackened earth on the leeward side of the tree tells of at least one campfire built from its remains.  Trampled grass makes paths to the southwest and southeast leading from the tree.

title: [[Darkmist Moor, Trail of Bones]]
description: The grass here is trampled around a great pile of decaying remains.  Femurs, skulls and skeletal hands lie in a heap with broken weapons and bits of rotting leather armor.  The trail of bones continues to the southwest and southeast, but whatever caused this carnage appears to have paused here for some time before moving on.

title: [[Darkmist Moor]]
description: A solitary dead tree, bleached white by the sun, still reaches its limbs high above the brown, lifeless patch of earth surrounding it.  Dozens of kobold skulls hang from the branches, suspended from ropes woven from the blades of the grass that is so abundant in the moor.  A hollow knocking sound is emitted by the skulls as they swing against each other in the wind.

title: [[Darkmist Moor, Trail of Bones]]
description: The trail dips gently into a fog-filled depression.  A small underground spring trickles from the rocks, making the ground along the trail spongy and wet.  The damp mist clings to everything, muffling sound and limiting sight to a few yards in any direction.

title: [[Darkmist Moor]]
description: Pale yellow weeds compete with the grass of the moor for the dim sunlight that filters through the mist.  A small patch of briars curls its thorny fingers over a large rock jutting from the ground.  To the east, the mist thickens into a dense fog, while to the south, the moor can be seen stretching away with only the occasional tree to mark the distance.

title: [[Darkmist Moor, Trail of Bones]]
description: A flat grey rock stretches across the path, briefly interrupting the gruesome ivory trail.  The tall dark green grass moves slightly in a gentle breeze, providing the only sign of life in this otherwise still expanse.  Off to one side, a decaying kobold head sits atop a crudely carved post -- a sacrifice, perhaps, or a warning.

title: [[Darkmist Moor, Trail of Bones]]
description: A small hip bone juts from beneath one of several low bushes that grow clumped together several feet from the trail of bones.  Amidst the long sharp thorns and tiny bright red berries rests a long solitary branch, its bark darker and more coarse than the bushes' slender stems.

title: [[Darkmist Moor]]
description: A half-buried boulder interrupts the game trail, its jagged surface covered in more of the blue-grey lichen that seems to flourish on the rocks of the grassland.  A rusted spearhead wedged deeply into the stone attests to the violence that once swept over this area.

title: [[Darkmist Moor]]
description: Crushed grass and a broken sword half buried in the ground give evidence of a violent struggle some time ago, though what became of the combatants remains a mystery.  A game trail loops from the northeast and northwest, but little else of note is apparent in the sea of grass rolling out in all directions.  Even the gentle rustling of the grass is muted by the dampness of the air.

title: [[Darkmist Moor]]
description: A gnarled tree huddles in the grass.  Its branches have been peppered with small arrows, and claw marks scar the trunk.  Within the branches, the dull glint of a helm can be spotted through the leaves.  Whatever creature it was that sought safety in the tree's arms apparently did not find it here.

title: [[Darkmist Moor, Nightshade Tangle]]
description: Sinuous tendrils of dark purple mist swim through the air, entangling themselves in the deformed limbs of barren trees like ethereal serpents.  The dusky scent of nightshade carries over the moor.

title: [[Darkmist Moor, Nightshade Tangle]]
description: Irregular patches of tall grass and squat shrubs lie beneath a sinuous blanket of dark purple mist.  The twisted shadow of an occasional barren tree looms in the foggy distance.

title: [[Country Church, Church Foyer]]
description: Though this narrow vestibule is small, it is crowned by a lovely high ceiling from which dangles the remains of a shattered chandelier.  Its walls are lined with old, faded portraits smudged with dirt.

title: [[Country Church, Main Hall]]
description: One large room comprises the church's sanctuary.  Simple pine pews line both sides of a tiny center aisle that leads to an altar to the north.  Small stained glass windows depicting woodland scenes adorn the walls on either side of the pews.

title: [[Country Church, Altar]]
description: All that adorns this understated altar is a faded white linen cloth.  The wooden planks underfoot are well worn from years of use, and they creak softly with each shift of weight.

title: [[Country Church, Cleric's Office]]
description: Barely furnished, this quiet office was designed for resident clerics to prepare for ceremonies.  A small table with a matching chair is pushed against one wall.

title: [[Country Church, Cloakroom]]
description: Ornate brass hooks adorn the walls where clerical vestments once hung.  The air is hot and choked with dust thanks to the lack of any appreciable ventilation.

title: [[Country Church, Short Hallway]]
description: Barely five feet long, this short hallway is separated from the sanctuary by a gracefully carved railing, leading to a narrow alcove at its eastern end.

title: [[Country Church, Statue Alcove]]
description: A tall wooden statue of Hodierna stands resolutely upon a painted column, staring blankly ahead.  There is an inherent darkness in this corner of the church, which cloaks the details of the architecture and bathes the mirthless statue in perpetual gloom.

timeto.13450: ;e if (DRStats.guild == 'Cleric' && DRSpells.known_spells['Resurrection']) then 20.0 else nil end

title: [[Country Church, Back Porch]]
description: Cracked and splintered boards, making a poor excuse for a porch, lead to a faded white door at the back of this forlorn little church.  A dirt path runs parallel to the damaged planks, leading northwest toward a cemetery.

title: [[Country Church, Cemetery Approach]]
description: A rickety porch nestled in the overgrown grasses of the moor provides entry to the back door of the dilapidated old church.  A scraggly dirt path heavily draped with weeds meanders northeast, approaching a long-forgotten cemetery.

title: [[Country Church, Cemetery Gate]]
description: Shattered remnants of an ancient iron gate flank the faint dirt pathway to either side, no longer hindering passage into the cemetery.  Thick weeds and vines slither into the once intricate latticework, vying for a higher perch on which to bask.

title: [[Country Church, Cemetery]]
description: Visible a short distance to the south, a modest mausoleum of grey granite rises out of the grassy moor.  The weed-ridden dirt pathway snakes eastward, making a wide arc through the cemetery and around to the structure.

title: [[Country Church, Cemetery]]
description: A faint dirt path wends southeast through a morbid garden of weatherworn tombstones.  Scraggly grasses push up through the ground above the ancient plots, creeping their way across the path.

title: [[Country Church, Cemetery]]
description: The dirt path bends sharply at the foot of a haggard hangman's tree, which bows beneath the weight of the souls it has reaped.  Several large stones scattered amidst the weeds and grass form erratic patterns.

title: [[Country Church, Cemetery]]
description: Monstrous gargoyles herald your approach to the granite mausoleum to the northwest, sneering wickedly at those that cross the dusty dirt path.  An ornate gold-veined marble tombstone lurches out of the ground just south of the path, marking the resting place of some noble of long ago.

title: [[Country Church, Before Mausoleum]]
description: The faint path turns into a round patch of grassless dirt before a pair of great obsidian doors that safeguard entrance to the grey granite mausoleum.  Unlike the rest of the pathway, the dirt here is free of the omnipresent weeds and grass, as if recent movement had discouraged their growth.  Gargoyles perched within high niches flanking the doors leer ominously down at all below.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Foyer]]
description: Strands of silver shoot through the black marble laid into the floor of the temple, spinning out across the glossy floor like the webs of some elaborate and unseen spider.  Shadows fall like curtains from the walls, concealing alcoves and small niches where statues of gods take residence.  Further down the hall to the north the darkness deepens as it allows access to the main hall of the temple.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Hall]]
description: The ceiling of the main hall climbs up in a steep curve of black marble.  Light from an unseen source shoots up out of ledges on the long sides of the hall, glancing off the facets of small diamonds that have been embedded in the vaulted roof.  The distant echo of someone crying softly carries through the narrow hall, coming from deeper in the darkness that lies to the north.
paths: Obvious exits: north, east, south, west.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Gela Erorien]]
description: On the wall opposite the doorway, a panoramic mural shows a red sun setting behind distant mountains to the west of Shard.  Painted clouds on the wall and ceiling shade from cream to rose as the sky around them blends imperceptibly from crimson to the indigo overhead to the velvet black of the eastern wall.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Gela Wepaten]]
description: At first glance, the room seems an open space beneath a starry sky: the dim light and the dull black of the walls merge into a dimensionless space in the center of which candles glow on a black altar.  Their light reflects from hundreds of tiny silvered points on the ceiling.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Hall]]
description: A ring of white marble sits in the dead center of the main hall.  Blindingly white, the ring seems almost to be there to bind the darkness that permeates the whole of this holy place.  Corridors to the east and west lead off into separate wings, their exact terminus lost in the darkness that cloaks the expanse of the temple.  The flickering of candles illuminate the way to the north and south, teasing the eye with the promise of more light.
paths: Obvious exits: north, east, south, west.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Western Alcove]]
description: A stone carving rises up out of the smooth face of the wall at the end of this alcove like some strange wave breaking the surface of a frozen obsidian waterfall.  The only illumination is the light coming from the main hall to the east, which is itself only fitful at best.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Eastern Alcove]]
description: A dark portal has forced itself upon the wall at the end of this alcove, the edges pulling at the black marble and drawing it close in a swirling embrace of greys and obsidians.  To the west, fleeting, sickly illumination attempts to break through the eternal night of the temple.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Grand Chamber]]
description: Corridors shoot out in all directions, a spider's maze of passages.  Wax splotches the floor in the center of the hall where the candles fixed in a wooden chandelier overhead have dripped down and frozen on the chilly marble.  Mixed sounds of chanting and weeping echo through the hall, a cacophony of cruelty multiplied tenfold by whatever dark architect designed the chamber to echo the world's sorrows with such crystal-clear clarity.
paths: Obvious exits: north, northeast, southeast, south, southwest, northwest.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Hall of Agony]]
description: Cries of pain echo through the hall, rising from soft to loud before crashing back down to a whimper.  Engravings of various scenes of torture from the past of Ilithi twist their way out of the wall, evoking a macabre sense of fascination to the casual eye.  The lighting is brighter here, intentionally harsh to cause a strain on the eyes and a nagging headache on the brain.
paths: Obvious exits: north, southeast, south, west.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Dergati's Alcove]]
description: No permanent light fixtures have been set up anywhere in honor of the goddess of true darkness.  Despite this, there is a definite air of tidiness -- someone has been polishing the floors and walls, and making sure that not a speck of dust mars the alabaster statue of Dergati that rests to the rear of the small shrine.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Aldauth's Alcove]]
description: Larger than the other alcoves in deference to the god of dark endings, most of the space is wasted since the only permanent fixture is a small black altar in the center of the rectangular room.  The air is neither hot nor cold, and there is no discernable fragrance.  Stripped down to the bare black marble floor, walls and altar, this is a quiet statement of just what we take with us when Aldauth pays his final visit.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Hall of Death]]
description: A lingering chill slips from between the seams of the walls and the glossy black floor, calling up the memory of aching bones in winter time.  The faint scent of burning blood and the taste of salt and copper hang in the air, tickling the senses like a finger applied to the back of the throat.
paths: Obvious exits: northeast, south, west, northwest.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Harawep's Alcove]]
description: This alcove is almost completely entombed with strands of sticky white cobwebs.  A draft ruffles some of the webbing, which all but covers the statue of Harawep huddled in the back of the tiny room.  Peering out from behind a veil of spidersilk, the hunched goddess glares and clutches a set of knitting needles.  The uncomfortable presence of shadowy movement near the back reveals a nest of black widow spiders who keep the walls and ceiling well-shrouded.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Glassus' Shop]]
description: The walls and floor of this sparsely furnished but clean room are of gold-veined white marble.  A series of immaculate countertops displays a variety of god-related artwork.  The proprietor of the shop, a smiling grey-cloaked monk by the name of Glassus, can often be found at his desk casually plucking the feathers from a dead and bloody pigeon.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Zachriedek's Alcove]]
description: The sour smell of vinegar and the musty odor of molding bread fill the air of this small and stuffy alcove.  A glowering, hunched-over relief of Zachriedek pops out of the wall furthest from the hall, his features rough from an unkind artist's chisel.  Fine cracks seam his face and body, as if it were about to crumble.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Kerenhappuch's Alcove]]
description: An ivory statue of Kerenhappuch in full skirt and low-cut blouse is located at the end of this alcove, the lighting at her feet and casting interesting shadows, especially around her chiseled eyes, which dance in the wicked light.  Gold leaf has been applied to her hair, and cinnamon incense cones lie burning at her feet, filling the air with a heady, spicy odor.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Hall of Madness]]
description: Faint giggling and the definite scent of overly powerful incense floats in through a set of appallingly gawdy draperies over an alcove to the north.  The acoustics of this part of the temple are good -- almost painfully so as they amplify the sound of desperate laughter in a steady flurry that borders on cacophony.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Hall of Vengeance]]
description: Crossed broken swords ornament the walls, side-by-side with the rent and rusted armor of those who have taken the oath of blood in the name of justice.  Torches flicker in sconces, casting shifting, churning light over everything but never quite reaching the ceiling.  There is a musty scent here, like that of stagnation.
paths: Obvious exits: north, east, southeast, southwest.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Botolf's Alcove]]
description: The quality of light is dim and fuzzy here, as if some sort of thick miasma obfuscates your vision no matter which way you turn your gaze.  A figure in shining armor stands at the back of the alcove, a mighty two-handed weapon clasped point-down against its chest.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Huldah's Alcove]]
description: The air is filled with a static feel, like a thunderstorm waiting to burst.  Veins of dark blue lapis shoot through the floor and walls, flashing like streaks of lightning.  The statue of Huldah that stands here is shaped from solid iron and plated in copper that is gradually growing greenish with age.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Ushnish's Alcove]]
description: Carnelian bands of gypsum twist like snakes in the floor here, writhing as they move up to the statue of Ushnish at the back of the room.  The granite statue of the god of treacherous rage is uncharacteristically calm in this carving, his serpentine eyes gazing quietly down and his hands folded in front of him as he clasps his famous iron-shod staff.  There is a deep sense of solitude here, as if the alcove were located miles below the earth.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Asketi's Alcove]]
description: A hearth is sunk into the floor in the center of this dim and chilly alcove, ashes from a long-dead fire spreading across the bottom.  A draft as chill as the north wind Asketi rides swirls through the air, rustling the various withered flowers and decomposing apples that are offered here in hopes of appeasing the cruel goddess.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Be'ort's Alcove]]
description: Unnerving silence fills this small and mostly unextraordinary alcove.  The only point of interest here is the statue of Be'ort that huddles in the back.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Drogor's Alcove]]
description: The tang of salt hangs in the air, coming from the saltwater-filled fountain in the center of the alcove.  A glowering statue of Drogor as his Gor'Tog self stands in the center of the fountain, up to his mid-calves in water.  A small shark swims through the water, preying on the tiny gobbets of flesh that are dropped in by the local priests.

title: [[Temple of Darkness, Trothfang's Alcove]]
description: This shrine is completely bare of any form of ornament or decoration.  Not even a statue graces the alcove, the only permanent fixture being a brass brazier on a tripod in the center.  The scent of burning flesh and the faint tang of copper hangs in the air, the subtle taste of the god of pain.

title: [[Shard, Temple of Light]]
description: Gold-veined white marble columns set upon square gilt bases support an arching roof with a fresco depicting the final battle between the Immortals and the World Dragon.  Hushed voices echoing from hidden alcoves soothe all who enter with melodious chants.  Candles burning in niches lining the walls between the pillars provide soft illumination.  A pair of embossed silver doors leading out onto the street stand wide open.

Light from candles set in wall niches reflects off gold-veined white marble columns to relieve the night's shadows.  Hushed voices chanting an eternal lullaby filter from unseen alcoves.  A pair of embossed silver doors stands open just wide enough for a soul to slip through to the street.

title: [[Temple of Light, Gela Ortegunen]]
description: The four walls of the room to north, east, west, and south are painted with the vistas seen from the highest tower of the city.  The views recede from the foreground of the roofs of Shard at the bottom of the walls and lead the eye upward to a distant horizon in every direction.  The ceiling directly above a wooden altar shows a golden sun.

title: [[Temple of Light, Gela Arenen]]
description: The first sight on entering the room is the eastern wall, covered with a vast painting of the lands stretching to the east of Shard.  The other walls of the square room continue the panorama of views to the north, west, and south.  Above the horizon on the east wall, the rosy fingers of dawn reach toward the ceiling, across which the colors darken to a deep, velvety purple above the dim mountains on the western horizon.

title: [[Temple of Light, Grand Hall]]
description: An alabaster dome, inset with crystal prisms and held aloft by vaulted arches, soars above the polished tile floor.  Light filtering through the prisms creates a dancing multi-hued aurora high above the fountain.  Centered beneath the dome is a fountain bubbling with water stained by the colorful reflected light.  A series of detailed mosaic animal images symbolizing the deities paves the path between the fountain and surrounding arches.

title: [[Temple of Light, Terrace]]
description: A curved slate-paved terrace running the length of the temple stretches outwards from the building.  The terrace area is enclosed by a marble railing.  Wrought iron tables and chairs dot the terrace for those who wish to enjoy the view of the gardens below.

title: [[Temple of Light, Garden Archway]]
description: A gravel path lined with green ferns leads from the bottom of the steps to the garden entrance.  Creeping vines covered with delicate violet blooms cling to the archway and small urns with potted flowers line the sides of the path.

title: [[Temple of Light, Contemplation Garden]]
description: The gravel path winds from the archway to create a perfect circle.  Various medicinal herbs line the sides of the path, creating an aromatic border.  Inside the circle a low cut hedge, barely knee-high, forms an intricate maze ending at a sundial set in a tiny inner circle.

title: [[Temple of Light, Fountain of One]]
description: Elegant and austere, the Fountain of One is a circular pool sculpted from gold-veined marble.  Within the pool, partially submerged visages of the Immortals exhale plumes of water which meld to form a single spray rising to touch the aurora above.

title: [[Temple of Light, Dim Alcove]]
description: A single candle burns steadily on a long wooden table here.  The stone bench pushed up against it looks hard and cold, but a beautiful illuminated book lies open on the table's surface, beckoning those who seek the wisdom of the gods to sit and study.

title: [[Stormwill Tower, Entrance Hall]]
description: The entrance hall of Stormwill, unlike most other towers in Shard, is very plain and unassuming, function being more important than form to the two Guilds based here.  Twin arches, on opposite sides of the hall, lead east to the Empath's Guild and west to the Infirmary.  A dark stone staircase curves sinuously into the darkness overhead, leading to the areas of the Tower devoted to the Warrior Mage Guild.

title: [[Stormwill Tower, Infirmary]]
description: The Infirmary has been set up by the Empath's Guild as a courtesy to the citizens of Shard too poor to afford the services of the Hospital attendants.  Staffed by some of the Guild's most gifted members, the room is filled with cabinets and drawers holding items most necessary to tending the wounded.  A large plaque is set over the archway leading to the entrance hall, its bright gold sheen the most noticeable spot of color in the otherwise drab room.

title: [[Stormwill Tower, Empath Guild]]
description: The Guildmaster's office is decorated in soothing greens and blues, with splashes of gold here and there to add color.  A lush white rug covers the stone floor to muffle the echoes caused by the stream of Empaths rushing in to speak with their leader, who sits behind a large mahogany desk covered in ledgers and invoices.  Hung on a rod near the stone fireplace is a kettle of lemonroot tea, the Guildmaster's favorite drink.

title: [[Empath's Guild, Waiting Room]]
description: Chairs line the perimeter of the room, but there is nothing to do here but wait and endure.

title: [[Empath Guild, Library]]
description: Unlike most other libraries, this room contains much more than simple books and scrolls, although those can also be found on the shelf on the northern wall.  Charts and diagrams hang from every inch of the wall, and lie strewn upon the tables as well, detailing the skeletal and muscular systems of the various Elanthian races.  A large glass display case bears a to-scale replica of the S'Kra pelvis and tail bones, to help illustrate their fragility.

title: [[Empath's Guild, Examining Room]]
description: This room is one of the many set aside for triage and severe trauma arrivals.  In a corner, a Paladin is gallantly trying not to cry as she keeps her arm attached to her shoulder with the help of a comrade's steady hand, and the soft crying of a father holding the battered body of his moaning son plays grim music in the background.  Healers rush about anxiously, sorting out the critical from the mortally wounded, and hastily pulling sheets over those who only Urrem'tier's hand could cure.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, Courtyard]]
description: The gleaming white stone walls that surround Brickwell Tower rise high around the cobblestoned courtyard, blocking out all sounds of the city beyond save those that filter through the wrought-iron portcullis.  The Tower itself is dominated by two massive white ironwood doors that stand slightly ajar.  The cobblestones of the courtyard are scrubbed clean every day by a horde of servants employed for that purpose alone.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, Entrance Hall]]
description: The grand entrance hall of the Trader's Guild is tastefully decorated in silk rugs and tapestries created by the finest Elven weavers in the province.  Twin columns, carved with images of sailing ships riding the crest of a wave, rise from the marble tiled floor.  A white marble staircase which leads to the upper levels of the tower is hung with the standards of trading companies based in the city of Shard.
paths: Obvious exits: north, east, west, out.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, Dispatch]]
description: The vast dispatch chamber is filled with frantic activity as caravan after caravan is quickly assembled and led out a pair of massive white ironwood doors, accompanied by the howls and complaints of those who feel they should have been first.  A shipping clerk is huddled at a desk piled with a mountain of invoices, trying to keep warm as all the heat from the room is sucked out of the opening between the doors.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, The Pit]]
description: The chamber devoted to commodities trading is a hornet's nest of activity.  Expensive tapestries and marble balustrades go completely unnoticed by those intent on wringing the greatest profit from their ventures.  A long bench is set against the back wall for those Traders too aged to stand for great lengths of time.

title: [[Traders' Guild, Sales Returns]]
description: This small, cramped room is warm all season round due to the press of bodies that fill it.  A few traders in the back handle the complaints that enter here in a neverending stream, their weary faces fixed with happy smiles.  You can feel a twinge of sympathy for the poor souls who handle all that the unhappy world of customer service has to dish out, and marvel at the patience with which the clerks handle their situation.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, Guildmaster's Office]]
description: Rich forest-green velvet draperies are pulled back to frame a woven tapestry on the teak paneled wall.  Etched-glass lanterns hang from wrought iron hooks in each corner of the room.  A large teak desk dominates the chamber, with a matching high-back chair the only seating provided.  A battered hunter's bow hanging from a small shelf on the far wall is the only incongruous note in the decor.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, Trade Minister]]
description: The trade minister's room, from the thick wall hangings to the elaborately carved desk, is decorated in shades of night.  Even the stone floors have been darkened to a nearly black color, although it is impossible to tell if that was intentional, or merely the result of hundreds of Traders tramping through the door to receive their latest contract.

title: [[Stairwell, Second Floor Landing]]
description: The landing is carpeted in deep royal blue rugs.  A small silverwood stand rests in the middle of the landing, bearing a china vase filled with Kertigen's Treasure roses.  To the west, a row of ebonwood doors provide private chambers for those Traders who cannot afford the prices of staying at an inn.  Light from the open door of the Crystal Sparrow fills the hallway.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, Rosemist Suite]]
description: Covered in thick silver-grey carpet, the floor of the Rosemist Suite feels like the fantasy of walking on a cloud.  Vases filled with the rare variety of Watermist roses, those that grow only at the base of waterfalls, are scattered about the room, filling the suite with their gentle fragrance.  A large bed covered in grey silk sheets rests in the center of the room, its surface strewn with blushing pink rose petals.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, The Crystal Sparrow]]
description: Set up by the Trader's Guild, the Crystal Sparrow is a small inn for those who are too busy with Guild business, or too tired from their travels, to visit one of the city's many finer establishments.  The stone walls of the room have been covered by cherrywood paneling carved with various images in sylvan theme.  A small crystal sparrow sits on display in a golden cage hung from the center of the ceiling.  A few tables are scattered around the room, spaced to provide privacy for the inn's patrons.

title: [[Stairwell, Third Floor Landing]]
description: The third floor landing is decorated in tasteful shades of green, from the forest carpeting to the sea-foam paneling on the walls.  A small white oak stand, inlaid with gold seashells, bears a crystal vase filled with Eluned's Tears.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, Lounge]]
description: The guild lounge, the walls paneled in cherrywood and the floors covered by a thick red carpet, is a place for guildmembers to relax and talk away from the driving concerns of profit.  Dominated by a huge oak bookcase, the room is filled with an air of calm relaxation, reinforced by the flickering light from the marble fireplace.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, Watersong Suite]]
description: A cunning network of pipes runs along the ceiling of the room, carefully hidden behind the same blue silk draping that covers the walls and the surface of the large four-poster bed in the center of the room.  As water runs through the pipes, they vibrate with a low hum.  Each pipe has a different tone, creating a virtual symphony of glorious song.

title: [[Brickwell Tower, Stargazer's Loft]]
description: A large glass dome surrounds the top of Brickwell tower, providing privacy for those who wish to be alone to gaze at the glory of the heavens above.  A large black stone fireplace rests at one end of the loft, filling the room with warmth.  Covered in black silk sheets sprinkled with bits of silver, a large bed rests near the fireplace.

title: [[Liani's Heaven, Entrance]]
description: The sound of laughter and gossip fills the air, mingling with the scent of pipe smoke and baking tarts.  A warm golden glow fills the room, coming from the north and the famous tavern of Liani's Heaven.  Pegs line the walls as places to hang cloaks and hats.

title: [[Liani's Heaven, Taproom]]
description: The golden glow of the polished walls is brightened by the fire of a hearth in the north wall.  Slow eddies of curling smoke twist into convoluted shapes as Elven elders and Halfling greybeards alike sit and smoke pipes, discussing the parts of life that yet remain a mystery, with tankards of ale before them to help make things more profound.

title: [[Liani's Heaven, Taproom]]
description: Light shimmers off the honey-colored wood that composes the low-roofed but expansive taproom of Liani's Heaven.  A bar curves from one end of the tavern to the other, its surface polished to a high gleam by tankards and plates slung down its surface by the Halflings behind the bar.

title: [[Liani's Heaven, Quiet Booth]]
description: A dark amber tabletop with heavy nicks and scoring occupies most of the booth.  A single lantern hangs overhead, throwing a pool of illumination over the padded benches provided for the comfort of the patrons who want a little peace and quiet to discuss business affairs best left to private places.

title: [[Liani's Heaven, Barman's Area]]
description: The service area of the bar is a hive of Halfling activity.  Dishwashers, ragmen, sweepers, and servers stream in and out of the bar's pass-through, all under the watchful eyes of the tavern bouncers.

title: [[Liani's Heaven, Small Room]]
description: Several musical instruments are carefully laid out on a low, felt-covered table.  An ancient grandmotherly Halfling woman glances up whenever anyone enters, and her gnarled fingers lovingly grasp a carved ivory flute.

title: [[Liani's Heaven, Private Table]]
description: A holdover from a time when wearing the symbol of the Bard's Guild was a death sentence and secrecy was necessary, this private table has now become a permanent fixture of the tavern as a reminder of those times.  Scrolls are laid out on the table, the elegant mark of a skilled calligrapher across their surface.

title: [[Golden Phoenix, Front Desk]]
description: Two brass lamps topped with stained glass shades rest on a carved rosewood check-in desk where a supercilious-looking clerk watches the lobby.  The walls are covered with gold damask, tasseled silk cords hold velvet drapes away from leaded windows and wing chairs upholstered with figured satin sit around a low carved table.  A plaster molding relief of intertwined flowers and leaves decorates the ceiling and wool runner carpets protect the polished wood floor.  A heavy oak door leads out to the street.

title: [[Golden Phoenix, Tavern Room]]
description: The sharp scent of spices overlays the yeast of baking bread and the savor of roasting meats.  Sunlight sparkles off cut-glass decanters and gleaming china on immaculate linen tablecloths. Pale yellow rosebuds in crystal vases are placed on each table along with a leather-bound menu, and gold flatware place settings are meticulously laid out, ready for the guest's dining pleasure.  Booths nestled against the walls allow for privacy, or guests can choose to sit at a table.

title: [[Golden Phoenix, Corridor]]
description: Delphiniums mixed with green fern fill a glazed blue urn sitting upon a metal stand, and the walls are covered with azure and gold striped paper topped with gilded moulding.  Brass rods hold the runner carpet covering the stairs in place and the aroma of lemony beeswax polish lingers about the rosewood bannister.

title: [[Golden Phoenix, Bar]]
description: A massive rosewood bar runs the length of one wall, its surface polished to a high gloss.  Behind the bar are rows of glasses, bottles and decanters stacked on shelves within easy reach of the bartender.  Tables dot the room, ample space is left between them to allow for privacy.  A young couple dances as a bard sitting on a small platform plucks a spritely tune from his mandolin.

title: [[Golden Phoenix, Trophy Room]]
description: Brass candle sconces vie for space with dozens of antlers, some still attached to the hunted's head, on the paneled walls.  Centered between the two largest trophies is a portrait of an Elothean man, while the opposite wall is decorated with a tapestry depicting a boar hunt.  Two overstuffed sofas face each other across a low table set with a decanter and brandy snifters, ready for afterdinner conversation.

wayto.51610: ;e fput('turn brass sconce'); move('go panel door')

title: [[Golden Phoenix, Hallway]]
description: The upper hallway is decorated with the same azure and gold striped paper and gilded moulding as in the lower corridor.  A glass frame holding a colorful pressed flower arrangement hangs opposite a marble statue atop a metal stand.

title: [[Golden Phoenix, Hallway]]
description: The azure and gold striped paper and gilded moulding continues throughout the hallway.  A mirror held by a gilded metal frame embellished with sculpted roses hangs on the wall at the end of the corridor.

title: [[Tower of Honor, Entryway]]
description: The broad, half-moon shaped entryway to the Paladin's Guild of Shard is made of the same creamy white marble substance that composes its exterior.  Veins of silver flash along the floor and sides, gliding around the doorway like fixed streaks of power.  Stairs carved out of the west wall ascend to the next brightly lit level.  To the north and through an arch cut in the wall that divides the entryway from the second half of the tower's base, is the office for the Shard guildleader.

title: [[Tower of Honor, Forge Tunnel]]
description: Sitting at the bottom of the long stone stairway that leads up to the Tower of Honor, this narrow hall holds no adornment.  The surrounding rock of the walls and ceiling has been expertly excavated, its surface smooth to the touch.  Well-placed torches generate some light, enough to see the way by.

title: [[Tower of Honor, Forge Tunnel]]
description: Sitting at the bottom of the long stone stairway that leads up to the forge, this narrow hall holds no adornment.  The surrounding rock of the walls and ceiling has been expertly excavated, its surface smooth to the touch.  Well-placed torches generate some light, enough to see the way by.

title: [[Tower of Honor, Guildleader's Office]]
description: Flanked by long tapestries of gold and blue, the guildleader's office is at once magnificent and sparse.  Illumination from crystal globes throws off a cool, silvery radiance, their placement and subsequent lighting automatically draws attention toward the polished white ironwood desk at the far back and center of the chamber.  A sense of pride and accomplishment infuses itself into the very air.  This is, indeed, the heart of the protectors of Ilithi.

title: [[Tower of Honor, Library Level]]
description: This room is but a small, semi-circular alcove with a doorway in the east side leading into the library of the paladins.  A set of stairs -- chiseled out of the white stone of the tower -- are located directly across from the doorway, climbing up one way, down the other.

title: [[Tower of Honor, Squire's Level]]
description: A doorway in the east side of this crescent-shaped alcove grants access to the barracks of the younger members of the Paladin's guild, also called the "Squire's Quarters".  A guard by the oaken door entryway monitors those who arrive and exit, and stairs on the wall across from her lead up toward the senior Paladins' quarters and training floor, and down toward the library and the entry level.

title: [[Tower of Honor, Knight's Level]]
description: The ends of this small alcove have been hung with banners dyed in the gold and blue colors of the Paladins of Shard.  A door of good steel in the east wall is watched over by a guard and a flight of stairs on the wall across from him lead up to the Justiciars' quarters and the training floor, and down toward still more quarters and the entry level.

title: [[Tower of Honor, Justiciar's Level]]
description: Bas-relief murals of blue lapis and goldstone have been set at either ends of this alcove in honor of those who have reached this level of excellence in the guild.  A door made of the same creamy white marble that composes the rest of the tower leads into the finest of the barracks, flanked at all times by two Paladins dressed in shining silvery plate.  Stairs lead up to the training floor, and back down to the lower quarters and the entryway.

title: [[Paladins' Guild, Justiciar's Study]]
description: The office of the Justiciar is plain, balancing on the knife edge between spartan and severe.  Nothing but a clean whitewash adorns the walls, except for the east one which has a single red dot painted on it, oddly enough.  A simple desk of uncarved wood is pushed up against the back, the papers on its surface in neat, regimented order.

title: [[Tower of Honor, Orb Room]]
description: Cold stone walls crowd close in this cramped chamber.  The room is barren save for a beautifully crafted soulstone orb mounted on a brass tripod, standing directly in the center of the alcove.

title: [[Tower of Honor, Library]]
description: The soft scent of sandalwood fills the air from the aromatic woods that have been used to make the shelves in the guild's library.  Not a speck of dust can be detected anywhere in the room, possibly due to the fact that the cleaning of this place is a primary chore of the younger initiates of the guild.  Curtains of heavy blue velvet gathered by gold cord frame stained glass windows that have been set in the four cardinal points of the circular walls.

title: [[Greenwalls Tower, Arrow Range]]
description: As you look about, you wonder for a moment just what the lunatics out at the far end of the field are doing just standing there while apprentice Rangers shoot arrows at them, until you realize that this is Shard's idea of agility training.  You do note to only minor relief that the bows in use appear to be lightly strung, the arrow tips padded against severe puncture damage.

title: [[Wyvern Arena, Triage Area]]
description: The cold stone floor of this room slopes slightly toward a rough metal trough, allowing for good drainage and easy cleaning.  Heavy wrought iron cots are arranged at intervals along the back wall.  Standing sentinel over each cot, large brass lamps provide excellent lighting for the healers and attendants.

title: [[Fever Point Pier, Lower Cross-bracing]]
description: The lower joints of the wooden cross-bracing smell like rotted fish and are slippery with bird droppings.  Several feet up, the upper cross-bracing runs just below the heavy beams supporting the pier's plank decking.  Looking below, the sandy beach emerges from beneath its rocky covering and winds in a lazy arc away from the piling toward a line of trees.

title: [[Fever Point Pier, Upper Cross-bracing]]
description: Additions, both man-made and natural, have been added to the original builders' work over the years.  One beam-end has a crude picture etched into it: two crossed scimitars set above a star.  Twigs from dislodged nests are wedged into the pier's joints, and the whole structure has been eroded by brine.  The lower cross-bracing offers a way back to the beach, but with a little luck and talent, it might be possible to climb onto protruding pier decking above.

title: [[Langenfirth, Trail Above the Fens]]
description: Almost buried in the fallen pine needles that cover the area between Gwenalion Fens to the east and Seord'telgi Teorn to the north, this narrow path wanders westward towards the distant hills.  Small sounds of a village at sleep -- a baby's hungry cry, a dog barking, a lone door slamming -- are wafted by the wind and populate the forest with echoes.

title: [[The Crossing, Werfnen's Strole]]
description: Werfnen's Strole, the Path of Dreamers, leads from the glories of the High Temple to the renowned hospitality of Skalliweg Barrelthumper's Half Pint Inn, brightly lit to welcome any late traveler.  The jocular Halfling is known throughout all Elanthia as the consummate innkeeper.  Mouthwatering aromas and heart-gladdening songs waft out of the inn, while the soothing gurgling of the tributary to the south creates a poignant counterpoint to the uproar within.

title: [[The Iris Rim, Warrior's Shrine]]
description: This room is faced with polished deep red porphyry and is dedicated to those whose burden in life is blood and battle.  Burning steadily, two torches frame a small steel altar forged from broken weapons, and cast long finger-like shadows across the shards of glistening metal.  A simple porcelain bowl rests in the middle of the altar, its white surface stained copper by the many offerings of blood droplets the temple monks provide during their vigils.

title: [[Siksraja, Village Garden]]
description: Neatly furrowed and planted with only a small path down the center that leads to a row of taffelberry bushes, this large garden is divided into several sections.  Tilted against the fence and the back of a tiny hut, a small wood cart with a broken wheel holds wood buckets and gardening implements.  A small area has been set aside to ferment mulch, and a dark pile in the far corner buzzes with flies.

title: [[Siksraja, Village Garden]]
description: The garden slopes down toward the lake, and a few plants appear to be thriving in the water.  Rows, neatly tilled for crops, are edged with mounds of carefully blended manure, dirt and garden waste to create rich mulch.  Slightly different pale green spikes fill two plots, and it is hard to tell if the crop is onions or garlic.

title: [[Dzirta Nars, Entry Room]]
description: This large room has been divided by curtains which can be pulled back to allow for large meetings.  The area by the door is guarded by Gazlok, whose sole task is to ensure that only Rakash may enter.  His austere cot and trunk leave plenty of space for passage though his chair is often used by those interested in discussing Rakash history or filled with a crony helping him pass time.

title: [[Traders' Guild, Mercantile Library]]
description: Square, leather-covered tables with brightly burning lamps line this domed-covered chamber.  A stained glass skylight at the dome's center filters the light to a soothing softness.  A shelf of books and manuscripts describing theories of trade and economics, cabinets full of scrolls, and racks replete with detailed maps of all known trade routes of Elanthia form the Mercantile Library's collection.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: Visible over the top of the garden wall rises the far higher wall guarding the perimeter of the city.  The southwest-facing stones trap all available sunlight, and this area is normally several degrees warmer than the rest of the garden.  Brilliant flame-colored tiger lilies flourish year-round under the clement conditions, and in front of them, a tangle of lepradria orchids sends up delicate vivid yellow blooms.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: The high grey limestone garden wall to the north provides protection from storms, sheltering the plantings at its base from harsh winds and rains.  Flowers normally found in more tropical climes flourish in this little enclave, their exotic and tantalizing scents filling the air even when winter holds the rest of the world in its icy fangs.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: A towering linden tree rises high over the garden, a remnant of the forest rising over the city walls to the northeast.  The spreading branches have become a home for squirrels and birds, who have learned that the visitors beneath them frequently leave edible treats behind.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: Overlooking several wooden chaises that have been polished to a smooth shine by years of use, a row of cherry trees lines the space between the white gravel path and the garden wall.  An oddly shaped porcelain bird feeder hangs from the branches of one tree, and the area is usually filled with chirps and birdsong.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: Centered in the path of tiny white quartz pebbles, an ancient sugar maple has been lifesculpted to suggest the figure of a pale unicorn emerging from its trunk.  So subtle was the work of the ancient Elven masters that the image sometimes seems visible only from the corner of the eye, disappearing into bark, branches and leaves when looked at directly.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: A high stone wall to the west closes off this area from the traffic, noise, and smells of the city, providing a quiet oasis that protects and encourages many delicate flowers and herbs to flourish.  Small cottages seem to blend into the lush growth, becoming an integral part of a living whole rather than an intrusion upon it.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Gate]]
description: Towering flamethorn trees line the path to the west.  Their scarlet leaves contrast with the pale green of small weeping willows that stand on either side of a wrought-iron gate, sentinels keeping the bustle of the city streets away from the quiet peace of the gardens.  The whitewashed stones of the Empaths' Guild rise to the south, with lacy ivy tendrils tracing patterns across their shaded surface.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: Bounded on the south by the whitewashed stones of the Empaths' Guild, the white-graveled path wanders past small, neat cottages surrounded by well-tended plantings.  To the east, an ancient weeping willow tree looms protectively over the area, providing dappled shade and shelter.  A bronze sundial has been placed in the center of the white gravel path.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: A small grove of silverwillow trees shelters the homes clustered around it, and someone has slung a mesh hammock in between two well-spaced trunks.  An industrious colony of ants works away at building its anthill higher, well away from the homes in the area.

title: [[Willow Walk, Fountain]]
description: Randomly shaped leaves of verdigrised copper form a tall fountain in the middle of a large pool filled with water lilies, which is surrounded by a low garden of flowers and herbs that shifts in color with the seasons.  Benches shaped of polished copperwood are scattered about, inviting the weary passerby to sit and be soothed by the music of the water trickling its random way down from one copper leaf to another into the surrounding pond.
paths: Obvious paths: north, northeast, east, southeast, south, southwest, west, northwest.

title: [[Willow Walk, Willow Tree]]
description: The massive weeping willow tree for which the garden is named spreads its trailing branches toward the ground, veiling the area and swaying with every breath of passing breeze to both reveal and conceal.  Occasionally, the leaves part enough to allow a glimpse to the south of the Sorrow Garden in which the Empath Guild Leader stands, and the tall wrought-iron fence running between there and here.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: A tangle of cloudberry bushes has grown so lush and tall that those seeking to walk by must move to the edge of the path, pushing past their sturdy stems.  In season, the berries are gathered and made into both tasty foodstuffs, and a particularly sweet and intoxicating wine.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: Several of those living in this area have created a small but thriving vegetable garden.  All who pass by here help in caring for the plants, and are free to share in the bounty that it produces as the seasons turn.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: A sense of peace, of bustling and burgeoning life, pervades the gardens.  In all seasons, plants and creatures grow and bloom when it is their time to flourish, and die only when it is their time to make way.  With care and attention, the living things inhabiting this area thrive and multiply, with each having a valued and necessary place and purpose.

title: [[Willow Walk, Garden Path]]
description: The whitewashed walls of the Empaths' Guild and Hospital rise to the south, with a neat row of taffelberry bushes planted at their base.  To one side, surrounded by a well-tended bed of flowers, is an alabaster figurine of an Elven woman holding a human child.

title: [[Emmiline's Cottage, Porch]]
description: Swept clean of debris, the white porch stretches across the front of the cottage, protecting the entryway from the elements.  At one end is a small seating area with a swing, two chairs and a glass-topped table.  At the other is a wooden door to enter the cottage, polished to a high sheen and mounted with a frosted window.  The oval glass features an etching of a unicorn standing in a meadow with a small wren perched on its spiraling horn.

Dimly lit by the lantern in one window, the corners of the wide porch are veiled in shadow.  Dark shapes at one end vaguely resemble a table and seating area, while only a greyish oval window hints at where the door might be.

title: [[Emmiline's Cottage, Path]]
description: A white gravel path, speckled lightly with grey stone, winds leisurely to the painted steps of a moderately sized cottage.  Wrapped around the front of the cheery yellow building is a pillared porch with a small seating area, and the steps are flanked by flower beds and small shrubs.  Lace curtains shroud the windows at the front of the home, and a third window, etched and frosted, is mounted into the polished wooden door.

A path of white gravel winds through the darkness to the steps of a moderately sized cottage.  Dark shapes hunch on either side of the steps, outlined dimly by the lantern shining through white lace in one window.  The white porch rails and pillars are muted by the night, the porch furniture crouched like slumbering beasts.  A greyish oval glows from the center of the door.

title: [[Zaulfung, Chickee]]
description: Overturned crates, smashed alchemical equipment, and bones not yet bleached by the sun lay amidst the debris strewn about this wide platform which rises from the mire below on stout ironwood pilings.  A strange sigil the color of dried blood has been painted in the center of the chickee.

title: [[Mauriga's Botanicals, Salesroom]]
description: The clean, pungent scents of herbs, medicinal plants and dried flowers envelop you in the cheerful, soothing salesroom.  Mauriga the Botanist beams at you as she arranges bunches of stalks, leaves, roots and seeds hanging from cedar racks overhead in order to dry or concentrate their potent properties.  She sniffs at a vase filled with fragrant jadice flowers, picks the freshest one, and offers it to you.  You are sure her potions, salves and herbs must be of the highest quality.

title: [[Mauriga's Botanicals, Root Cellar]]
description: A stair carpeted with a richly patterned runner leads down to the root cellar when Mauriga prepares and preserves her concoctions, based on ancient clan and family recipes.  Raw materials fill jar after crystal jar, on niches in the earthen walls.  Always needful of ingredients, she happily buys herbs from adventurers and keeps them here as well.  A few serious-looking Elves and Eloths, and a snoozing Halfling, sit around a mixing table, fiddling with scales, scoops, and vials.

title: [[Cormyn's House of Heirlooms]]
description: The walls here of an odd white adobe, smeared with stucco that has been inlaid with broken bits of colored glass, mirror fragments and round disks of polished metal resembling coins.  This is obviously Cormyn's idea of elegance.  The merchandise that others have pawned, or that is awaiting redemption, seems to be mostly flotsam and jetsam.  Noting the huge ruby on Cormyn's finger, and the stout gold chain about his neck, it dawns on you that there may be more here than meets the eye.

title: [[Cormyn's House of Heirlooms]]
description: This private office is a welcome contrast to the front room of the Cormyn's pawnshop.  It appears to be a luxuriously appointed retreat for someone of great wealth and prominence.  Due to its quiet, tasteful decor, you are sure it must be someone other than Cormyn.  An ebony desk and a high-backed leather chair show signs of frequent use.  In the corner, a ceiling-high safe holds secrets to which you are not privy.

title: [[Milgrym's Weapons, Showroom]]
description: This is a plain and businesslike shop carrying a wide variety of weapons.  A fair assortment of the wide range of methods to cut, bash, crush, eviscerate and otherwise discomfit your enemies can be had here.  Traders with exotic or unusual weapons are welcome to come in and dicker as Milgrym has an eye for bargains and an appreciation of good weapons.

title: [[Berolt's Dry Goods, Storage]]
description: Except for a few dusty old crates and splintering barrels shoved up against one wall, this small, close room is bare.  On top of one barrel, someone's lunch of cheese and bread is awaiting their return, provided it survives the obvious interest of a tiny mouse, who is now snuffling among some of the larger crumbs.

title: [[Berolt's Dry Goods, Showroom]]
description: Rough walls and floors covered with a gritty layer of dirt attest to the constant traffic in what must be one of the more popular establishments in town.  Shelves and counters crowd together, displaying all manner of equipment for a rugged lifestyle in an orderly, if dustridden manner.  Berolt, the proprietor, keeps a close eye on business, but still manages a quick, hearty laugh at a rather bawdy joke from a coarse-looking character who is obviously a regular visitor here.

title: [[Falken's Tannery, Workshop]]
description: The Tannery, presided over by the ever-alert Falken, reeks of dead things, chemicals, and unwashed adventurers who rush in to sell or appraise their latest haul of skins and furs.  On the rough, deobar-paneled walls are mounted stuffed heads of animals, and specimens of birds and fish.  You are struck by the absence of stuffed reptiles, however.  On the counter lies a bundle of assorted furs and hides.

title: [[Falken's Tannery, Fitting Room]]
description: Here Falken personally fits you for your new hide, skin, fur or leather accoutrements.  A full-length sheet of metal, polished to a mirror-like finish, on the far wall reflects your image.  In the mirror's reflection, you also notice that the walls of the fitting room are hung with rare furs and exotic pelts, some of creatures you have only heard or dreamt about, but never seen.  On a cluttered worktable in the corner, awls, leather thongs and other tools of the trade are scattered about.

title: [[Falken's Tannery, Supply Room]]
description: Jars and bottles are neatly arranged on a number of well-made pine shelves affixed to the walls.  Several bins overflow with small tools and crude scrapers.  A bored clerk lounges on a stout chair behind a wide counter.

title: [[Falken's Tannery, Vat Room]]
description: Heaps of uncured pelts lie festering around a huge wooden vat at the center of the room.  Several young Gor'Togs, who seem oblivious to the stench, lumber about, tending to the tanning process.  Bubbles and fume spew forth from the vat each time they toss in a skin.  As you poke at a pile of hides awaiting tanning with your foot, you raise a storm of horseflies.

title: [[Taelbert's Inn, Lobby]]
description: Though many such inns dot the landscape, Taelbert's is known as especially hospitable to locals and wayfarers alike.  Here in the lobby, clerks busy themselves behind an antique mahogany counter, seeing to the needs of guests and directing the activities of the rather large staff.

title: [[Taelbert's Inn, Bar]]
description: Bursts of laughter and excited shouts ring out from a game of dice being played at a corner table.  Other tables and chairs are scattered haphazardly through the room, but most of the regulars perch on high stools near the bar.  Apparently, the view of the buxom barmaid is more enticing from that angle.

title: [[Taelbert's Inn, Dining Room]]
description: The spacious dining room is elegant, if slightly frayed at the edges.  Faded blue velvet chairs cluster around white linen-covered tables set with fine old silver and occasionally mismatched china.  Set between two pillars on the southwest wall, a curtained alcove offers privacy, and to the southeast, soft light spills outward from a quiet corner.

title: [[Taelbert's Inn, Hallway]]
description: At one time, this inn must have been a private home, which explains the relatively few rooms available for guests.  Several doors open up off this second floor hallway, which makes a sharp turn to the north at the far end.

title: [[Taelbert's Inn, Hallway]]
description: The north hall ends abruptly here at the quietest corner of the house.

title: [[Taelbert's Inn, Cozy Room]]
description: Though small in size, the room is comfortably furnished with a sturdy brass bed taking up much of the wall opposite the door, and a tiny desk tucked into one corner.  Thick braided rugs of deep green wool complement the walls, which have been painted a soft grey.

title: [[Taelbert's Inn, Blue Room]]
description: Sky blue walls and indigo carpets combine to give this room a cool, soothing atmosphere.  The mahogany four-poster bed is covered with a patchwork satin comforter in shades of green and turquoise, offering a striking counterpoint to the crisp white, lace-edged linens that peek out from underneath.

title: [[Half Pint, Grand Foyer]]
description: The two-story foyer of Skalliweg's Half Pint always seems crowded with jovial merrymakers coming and going.  All kinds gather here, but there is a noticeable predominance of Humans, Halflings and Dwarves.  An ornate wrought-iron spiral stair dominates the room, sweeping upwards to the second floor.  From a high archway to the east waft the sounds of good company and the smells of even better ale and victuals, and through some stout double doors to the south are heard roars of encouragement.

title: [[Half Pint, Dance Floor]]
description: A more recent addition to the Half Pint, the dance floor has a polished hardwood floor and a chandelier crafted from brushed silver and tiny blue crystals.  A strategic placement of mirrors makes the room seem bigger then it really is.  The musicians sit behind a decorated rail that keeps the dancers from accidentally falling into their beloved instruments.

title: [[Half Pint, Bards' Corner]]
description: In sharp contrast to the Main Saloon and more boisterous reaches of The Half Pint, this quiet chamber is softly lit and tastefully decorated with antique tapestries depicting famed minstrels and legendary troubadours from the annals of Elanthia.  The room itself has no tables and chairs, but rather a recessed wooden seating pit with overstuffed cushions scattered about the floor.  At the far end is a raised platform with a lectern, a low ottoman and a music stand.

title: [[Half Pint, Main Saloon]]
description: Skalliweg Barrelthumper, proud proprietor of The Half Pint, perches alertly on a high stool behind the sleek, polished bar, shouting at serving wenches, cooks and customers alike.  Patrons dine, drink, dispute and dream on, in spite of the constant hum, draped over comfortable rush-seated chairs or hunched over well-worn tables.  Faces flicker and eyes glimmer in the dim light of the wrought-iron chandelier and candle stubs sputtering in crocks on the tables.

title: [[Half Pint, Gaming Room]]
description: Here are gathered some of town's most serious gamblers, gamers and wagerers.  They cluster about a few round tables rolling dice, rattling bones and casting shells.  Several square tables bear cards, tokens, game pieces, and painted wooden boards with various runes and numbers on them.  You observe a curious fact: the round tables heaped high with gold are surrounded by tense faces, while the crowds around the square tables are laughing, joking, drinking and enjoying themselves immensely.

title: [[Town Hall, Debtors' Office]]
description: This large room is full of clerks processing citizens' and travellers' payments for the various debts, fines and taxes any town needs to operate.  A well-worn and scuffed counter keeps the public at bay from the harried civil servants and the tile floor is badly in need of waxing from the countless feet that have shuffled in and out during the day.  The room has that somewhat grim and cheerless feel common to most places where people are forced to hand over money.

title: [[Town Hall, Lobby]]
description: Surrounded by the nerve centers of the administrative arm of the local government, the lobby is an area open to the second floor with skylights in the roof overhead.  Various offices open off the main floor, and a flight of stairs leads upward.  An attempt at a cheerful paint scheme has become worn and faded with time until it is now a dusty grey and anemic beige, dull and unremarkable.

title: [[Crossing, Carousel Desk]]
description: A long wooden desk spans the width of the western wall.  Brass lanterns hang from the ceiling, and the floor behind the desk is covered in spotless red tile.

title: [[Crossing, The Carousel]]
description: Exotic tapestries of every possible description drape the wall ringing the Carousel's core.  A circular roof supports a vast framework of iron and timbers rising to the building's apex.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights within the structure form the strikingly complex and beautiful mechanism which drives the Carousel.

Exotic tapestries of every possible description drape the wall ringing the Carousel's core.  A circular roof supports a vast framework of iron and timbers rising to the building's apex.  Countless gears, pulleys and weights within the structure form the strikingly complex and beautiful mechanism which drives the Carousel.

title: [[Crossing, Carousel Square]]
description: A massive conical building rises from the cobbles at the square's center, its snowy alabaster surfaces gleaming brilliantly against the drab backdrop of the surrounding stone and wood.  A bejeweled mosaic set above an oval doorway reads "THE CAROUSEL."

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Northeastern Tunnel]]
description: The ground's incline is much more pronounced, though it doesn't seem to bother the slug-like creatures clinging to the cave's wall in the least.  A thick layer of slime blankets the remains of some type of barrier that once consisted of iron bars, rocks and wooden planks.  The debris is scatted towards the cave's exterior, as if something attempted -- and succeeded -- in breaking free of the damp-aired prison.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Northeastern Tunnel]]
description: Three neatly stacked piles of stones form a triangular pattern in the center of the pathway leading through the murky darkness.  The charred remains of several small limbs and larger logs are propped against the supporting structure.  A distorted metal charm lies half-buried in the black ash beneath the wood, melted to a degree so that only an equine profile can be made out.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Northeastern Tunnel]]
description: Thick, gnarled roots protrude from one side of the tunnel and create a tangled mess that makes traveling through it difficult.  Strips of leather and softer materials are interwoven in the writhing mass, each having been ripped from the garments of those who tried to pass through.  After brushing against one of the roots, it becomes clear why the passage is so difficult -- the roots have been petrified from countless years in the damp tunnels.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Northeastern Tunnel]]
description: Dagger-like stalactites protrude from the ceiling and reach halfway to the ground.  On the outer edges of the tunnel's ground are tiny bumps in the stone, either the early beginnings of stalagmite companions to their hanging counterparts or a natural deformation in the stone.  Small grains of a sand-like substance are piled around the bumps and seem to follow a barely discernible winding groove.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Northeastern Tunnel]]
description: A salty sea breeze moans loudly through a series of porous holes in sections of the tunnel's walls.  Somewhere further within the earthen tomb come the scuttling echoes of movement, though discerning any details about what the source may be is impossible through the moaning sea air.  Four sets of four deep scratches mar an area of sandstone on one wall, as if some creature had pounced off of it in a hasty pursuit or retreat.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Alcove]]
description: The secluded alcove opens up into a much larger complex of cavernous areas.  Four main pathways branch outwards, each forming an ovoid tunnel that vanishes into the murky darkness, though a mass of roots and a pile of bones obscure two of the passages.  A salty breeze from the southern exit occasionally pierces the stifling stillness of the cavern.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Northern Tunnel]]
description: A strong breeze sweeps down the tunnel, carrying with it the strong smells of the ocean and smoldering fires from the beaches.  The light from outside pierces the darkness just enough to provide a dim, grey illumination to the relatively smooth sandstone walls.  A small scene has been carved into one section of the wall, meticulously depicting a battle between humanoids and a many-armed creature.  The final image, presumably the outcome, remains unfinished.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Northern Tunnel]]
description: The shattered remains of a stone barricade fill the cave with chunks of rubble.  While many of the stones are barely more than a fine-grained sand, others are as large as a sturdy Dwarf.  Viciously deep claw marks line the cave's walls on either side of the barricade, leaving little doubt that the structure failed its purpose -- either holding something as prisoner or keeping outside forces from something believed to be well-protected.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Northern Tunnel]]
description: The ground is littered with bent pieces of rusted and twisted metal.  Some of the larger pieces show signs of having been ripped apart by claws or viciously sharp teeth.  Providing a stark contrast to the tattered remnants of the armor, a gleaming golden hilt with a small portion of a brilliant silver blade has been plunged deep into the cave's wall.  Large fractures in the sandstone around the weapon reveal a layer of granite that holds the blade fast into place.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Northern Tunnel]]
description: Propped against one side of the cave is a mostly intact suit of rusted plate armor, the skeletal remains of its owner still holding a broken sword in one of its boney hands.  Tangled between the fingers of the other is a mass of brownish fur.  A small phrase has been deeply scratched into the armor's surface, in memory of those who perished along with the warrior.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Northern Tunnel]]
description: The cave makes a sharp curve, almost turning back on itself entirely as it makes a considerable downward slope into the depths of the cliffs.  The walls are coated in a thick slime, and a fetid dampness lingers in the air.  What little outside air may stir through the tunnels near the entrance is entirely lacking in this portion of the cliffs' interior.  Inching along the lower levels of the walls are elongated, slug-like creatures that feast on the mucous substance.

title: [[Talas Sagamat, Underground Swamp]]
description: A large cavern opens up before you, almost perfectly divided between stagnant water and a wet, muddy mixture of sand and clay.  Both exits of the cavern rise steeply upwards, creating somewhat of a natural spillway to hold the water within.  Humanoid footprints cross with the markings of other creatures, some snake-like and others with prints similar to those of a dog, though considerably larger.  The water is marred by constant ripples and bubbles that emanate from the center.

title: [[The Shanty, Common Room]]
description: Airy and open with a hint of fried fish in the air, this place offers customers a place to relax, eat and chat in leisure.  Roughly woven nets decorated with seashells line the walls while large wooden picnic tables are set with tropical-themed placemats and colorful napkins.  Sweet scented candles grace the tables, ready to be lit when darkness falls.

title: [[Fang Cove, Dock]]
description: A hard stone walkway winds along the edge of the crystal waters that make up Fang Cove.  Standing in stark contrast to the crude structures within view, many colorful flowers liven up the otherwise drab community.  Here and there, bits of chipping paint can be seen on some of the huts.

title: [[Fang Cove, Dock]]
description: Crudely assembled yet sturdy just the same, the dock consists of parts of a ship's hull lashed together with bits of woven rope.  A single lantern hangs from a pole at the end of the structure, swaying with the beat of the waves lapping against the ballast below.

title: [[Fang Cove, Obsidian Dome]]
description: The austere building is crafted from geometrically exact blocks of red striated obsidian that form a perfectly cylindrical chamber broken only by an arched exit.  The crystalline dome above reveals the bright, cheery autumn sky.

title: [[Fang Cove, Walkway]]
description: In spite of the otherwise rundown appearances of the small community, a simple two-story building and its furnishings dominates the area near the cove's small pier.  A decorative pole displays a dragon-shaped lantern that remains unlit during the daylight hours while white wicker tables and chairs placed around the source of illumination provide a cozy atmosphere for social gatherings by the area's inhabitants.

Sweet aromas drift from the two-story building that dominates the area near the cove's pier.  A decorative pole holds a dragon-shaped lantern, its bright flame diligently flickering into the night.  Groups of inhabitants gather around white wicker chairs and tables beneath the illumination to talk of the day's happenings in the small community while others go inside for more comfortable arrangements.

title: [[Fang Cove, Walkway]]
description: A spiked-iron fence lines the walkway, keeping stray beasts and children from tumbling down the rocky outcrop below.  A gate to the west provides access to steps that lead to a thin strip of pale, sandy beach.  Someone has braided pink ribbon through a couple of the fence posts, leaving the ends to flutter in the breeze.

title: [[Fang Cove, Walkway]]
description: A decorative clay pot resting beside a sturdy iron gate holds a fragrant blue butterfly bush.  The gate itself is adorned with carvings of seahorses, shells and a single octopus and opens to some narrow steps.  Below, children chase one another calling out names and causing general mayhem among the adults present.

title: [[Fang Cove, Walkway]]
description: A simple wooden fence, crafted from the splintered remains of a ship's framework and barbed wire, lines the walkway to keep stray beasts and children from tumbling down the rocky outcrop below.  A long strip of pale sandy beach can be seen beyond a gate to the east.  A hearty dolphin vine weaves itself through the bars of the fence post, its fragrant blooms scenting the surrounding air.

title: [[Fang Cove, Walkway]]
description: A fairy wind-chime plays sweet tunes while passing travelers stroll by a tiny shop.  Pale ribbons stream from above its doors.  A wooden bench painted snow white sits beside the shop and opposite an iron-wrought gate that leads to the beach below.

title: [[Fang Cove, Fate's Fortune Lane]]
description: A towering marble archway opens a gap in the wall to the north and separates the ongoing construction and somewhat more refined completed structures of Fate's Fortune Lane from the crude structures and makeshift walkway along the beach.  The entrance to a squat, wide bungalow sits in opposition to the arch, and the sheltering cliffs of Fang's Peak rise up from behind it.  To either side of the arch, cobblestones of different shapes and sizes have been laid out to form the wide Fate's Fortune Lane.
